"""Investors respond quickly to the headline EPS surprise but are slower to assess whether the surprise is economically credible when consensus has been stale. A positive surprise corroborated by operating cash flow and stable working-capital quality should continue to drift upward, while a negative cash-confirmed surprise should drift downward. The signal should fail if post-release returns are equally strong for fresh and stale consensus names, or if cash-flow corroboration adds no incremental explanatory power beyond EPS surprise."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _aligned(frame: pd.DataFrame, anchor: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Defensively align a point-in-time field to the output panel."""
    return frame.reindex(index=anchor.index, columns=anchor.columns)


def _bars_since_estimate_change(
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal age, in bars, since either consensus estimate last changed."""
    eps_values = eps_estimate.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rev_values = revenue_estimate.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rows, cols = eps_values.shape
    ages = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    previous_eps = np.full(cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
    previous_rev = np.full(cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
    previous_active = np.zeros(cols, dtype=bool)

    for row in range(rows):
        current_eps = eps_values[row]
        current_rev = rev_values[row]
        active = np.isfinite(current_eps) | np.isfinite(current_rev)

        eps_changed = np.isfinite(current_eps) & (
            ~np.isfinite(previous_eps)
            | (np.abs(current_eps - previous_eps) > 1e-12)
        )
        rev_changed = np.isfinite(current_rev) & (
            ~np.isfinite(previous_rev)
            | (np.abs(current_rev - previous_rev) > 1e-12)
        )
        changed = active & (eps_changed | rev_changed)

        if row == 0:
            ages[row, active] = 0.0
        else:
            continuing = active & previous_active & ~changed
            ages[row, continuing] = ages[row - 1, continuing] + 1.0
            ages[row, active & ~continuing] = 0.0

        previous_eps = current_eps.copy()
        previous_rev = current_rev.copy()
        previous_active = active

    return pd.DataFrame(ages, index=eps_estimate.index, columns=eps_estimate.columns)


def _fundamental_update_mask(
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify report/update dates using only contemporaneous step changes."""
    actual_previous = eps_actual.shift(1)
    surprise_previous = eps_surprise.shift(1)

    actual_update = eps_actual.notna() & (
        actual_previous.isna() | (np.abs(eps_actual - actual_previous) > 1e-12)
    )
    surprise_update = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        surprise_previous.isna() | (np.abs(eps_surprise - surprise_previous) > 1e-12)
    )
    return actual_update | surprise_update


def _working_capital_growth(level: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing change in a balance-sheet level, clipped against tiny bases."""
    prior = level.shift(lag)
    denominator = prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((level - prior) / denominator).clip(-2.0, 2.0)


@register_factor
class StaleConsensusCashConfirmedSurprise(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks stale-consensus EPS surprises corroborated by cash-flow quality."""

    factor_id = "stale_consensus_cash_confirmed_surprise"
    name = "Stale-Consensus Cash-Confirmed Surprise"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "On fundamental-update dates, ranks signed EPS surprises scaled by "
        "consensus staleness and cash-flow confirmation, rewarding positive "
        "surprises with healthy conversion and negative surprises with weak "
        "cash quality."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "incomeQuality",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "netIncome",
        "receivables",
        "inventory",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        anchor = data["close"]
        eps_actual = _aligned(data["epsActual"], anchor)
        eps_surprise = _aligned(data["epsSurprise"], anchor)
        eps_estimate = _aligned(data["epsEstimate"], anchor)
        revenue_estimate = _aligned(data["revenueEstimate"], anchor)
        income_quality = _aligned(data["incomeQuality"], anchor)
        operating_cash_flow = _aligned(data["operatingCashFlow"], anchor)
        net_income = _aligned(data["netIncome"], anchor)
        receivables = _aligned(data["receivables"], anchor)
        inventory = _aligned(data["inventory"], anchor)

        update_mask = _fundamental_update_mask(eps_actual, eps_surprise)

        estimate_age = _bars_since_estimate_change(eps_estimate, revenue_estimate)
        staleness = (estimate_age / 126.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        estimate_scale = eps_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_surprise = (eps_surprise / estimate_scale).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        signed_surprise = (2.0 * rank(relative_surprise) - 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        cash_conversion = operating_cash_flow / net_income.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        conversion_component = cash_conversion.clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        quality_component = income_quality.clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        cash_quality = 0.5 * (conversion_component + quality_component)

        receivables_growth = _working_capital_growth(receivables, 63)
        inventory_growth = _working_capital_growth(inventory, 63)
        working_capital_drag = 0.5 * (receivables_growth + inventory_growth)

        cash_direction = np.tanh((cash_quality - working_capital_drag).fillna(0.0))
        cash_available = (
            income_quality.notna()
            | cash_conversion.notna()
            | receivables.notna()
            | inventory.notna()
        )

        agreement = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(2.0 * signed_surprise * cash_direction))
        confirmation = (0.25 + 0.75 * agreement).where(cash_available, 1.0)

        raw_score = signed_surprise * staleness * confirmation
        event_score = raw_score.where(update_mask)
        return rank(event_score).where(update_mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

"""A positive EPS surprise caused by unexpectedly strong revenue is more likely to represent persistent demand information than one caused solely by temporary cost control, tax effects, or accounting noise. Investors often initially anchor on the headline EPS beat, but revise medium-term sales and margin expectations more gradually when both revenue and EPS surprises confirm each other. The hypothesis is falsified if joint revenue-and-EPS surprises do not outperform EPS-only surprises after controlling for sector and announcement-period volatility."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_centered_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank each surprise within its sector and map ranks symmetrically to [-1, 1]."""
    clean_values = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNCLASSIFIED__")

    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    unique_labels = pd.unique(labels.to_numpy().ravel())

    for label in unique_labels:
        member_mask = labels.eq(label)
        sector_values = clean_values.where(member_mask)
        member_count = sector_values.notna().sum(axis=1)
        raw_rank = sector_values.rank(axis=1, method="average")

        midpoint = (member_count + 1.0) / 2.0
        half_range = ((member_count - 1.0) / 2.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        centered = raw_rank.sub(midpoint, axis=0).div(half_range, axis=0)
        centered = centered.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        result = result.mask(member_mask, centered)

    return result.fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class DemandLedSurpriseCompositionDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Demand-confirmed earnings surprises predict post-announcement drift."""

    factor_id = "demand_led_surprise_composition_drift"
    name = "Demand-Led Earnings Surprise Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Within-sector surprise composition score that rewards jointly large, "
        "same-direction revenue and EPS surprises while suppressing isolated "
        "or contradictory surprise channels."
    )
    window_length = 1
    inputs = ["revenueSurprise", "epsSurprise", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector = data["sector"]

        revenue_rank = _sector_centered_rank(revenue_surprise, sector)
        eps_rank = _sector_centered_rank(eps_surprise, sector)

        # A geometric joint magnitude makes an isolated channel neutral.  The
        # agreement term is one for matched ranks and declines to zero as the
        # two channels point in opposite directions.
        joint_magnitude = np.sqrt((revenue_rank.abs() * eps_rank.abs()).clip(lower=0.0))
        agreement = (1.0 - (revenue_rank - eps_rank).abs()).clip(
            lower=0.0, upper=1.0
        )
        direction = np.sign(revenue_rank + eps_rank)
        score = direction * joint_magnitude * agreement

        both_available = revenue_surprise.notna() & eps_surprise.notna()
        return score.where(both_available, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

"""The market frequently rewards reported sales growth before fully distinguishing internally funded expansion from growth purchased with dilution, leverage, or aggressive balance-sheet investment. Revenue acceleration supported by operating cash flow and stable-to-falling share count is a more credible growth regime, while growth accompanied by issuance, debt expansion, and rapid asset accumulation is vulnerable to repricing. The mechanism should fail if financing composition has no incremental explanatory power beyond revenue growth and sector membership."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _safe_rank(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally rank finite observations and assign neutral rank to gaps."""
    clean = value.where(np.isfinite(value), np.nan)
    return rank(clean).fillna(0.5)


def _cash_flow_conversion(
    operating_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame, revenue: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal point-in-time operating cash-flow conversion with bounded outliers."""
    denominator = revenue.where(revenue.abs() > 1.0e-12, np.nan)
    conversion = operating_cash_flow / denominator
    return conversion.where(np.isfinite(conversion), np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)


@register_factor
class SelfFinancedGrowthConfirmationDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks cash-supported growth while penalizing externally financed expansion."""

    factor_id = "self_financed_growth_confirmation_drift"
    name = "Self-Financed Growth Confirmation"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral cross-sectional score for revenue and operating-cash-flow "
        "growth confirmed by cash conversion, less dilution, debt growth, and asset "
        "growth associated with externally financed expansion."
    )
    window_length = 1
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "revenueGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "revenue",
        "sharesGrowth",
        "debtGrowth",
        "assetGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]

        revenue_growth = data["revenueGrowth"].where(
            np.isfinite(data["revenueGrowth"]), np.nan
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        cash_flow_growth = data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"].where(
            np.isfinite(data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"]), np.nan
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        conversion = _cash_flow_conversion(
            data["operatingCashFlow"], data["revenue"]
        )

        shares_growth = data["sharesGrowth"].where(
            np.isfinite(data["sharesGrowth"]), np.nan
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        debt_growth = data["debtGrowth"].where(
            np.isfinite(data["debtGrowth"]), np.nan
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        asset_growth = data["assetGrowth"].where(
            np.isfinite(data["assetGrowth"]), np.nan
        ).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        growth_confirmation = (
            0.35 * _safe_rank(revenue_growth)
            + 0.25 * _safe_rank(cash_flow_growth)
            + 0.20 * _safe_rank(conversion)
        )
        external_financing = (
            0.10 * _safe_rank(shares_growth)
            + 0.05 * _safe_rank(debt_growth)
            + 0.05 * _safe_rank(asset_growth)
        )
        raw_score = growth_confirmation - external_financing

        sector = data["sector"].where(data["sector"].notna(), "Unknown")
        sector_neutral_score = indneutralize(raw_score, sector)
        signal = _safe_rank(sector_neutral_score) - 0.5
        return signal.reindex_like(template).fillna(0.0)

"""An analyst-consensus revision is most actionable when it has not yet been absorbed into the stock price, especially when it is idiosyncratic rather than a broad sector-wide revision that attracts immediate attention. This is a conditional factor-timing implementation: the estimated-revision signal is scaled down in high-breadth revision regimes and amplified for isolated revisions with weak sector-relative price confirmation. The mechanism is falsified if recent sector-relative returns already fully incorporate subsequent analyst-estimate changes, or if revision breadth does not condition the signal's realized spread."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cross-sectional sector normalization for each observation date."""
    sector_values = sector.reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    grouped = values.T.groupby(sector_values.iloc[0], sort=False)
    # Sector labels are static, but use each column's supplied label defensively.
    labels = sector_values.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in labels.dropna().unique():
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        subset = values.loc[:, columns]
        mean = subset.mean(axis=1)
        std = subset.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        result.loc[:, columns] = subset.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0)
    return result


def _sector_relative_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing stock return less the equal-weighted trailing sector return."""
    cumulative = ret.fillna(0.0).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    labels = sector.reindex(index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns).ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for label in labels.dropna().unique():
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        sector_return = cumulative.loc[:, columns].mean(axis=1)
        result.loc[:, columns] = cumulative.loc[:, columns].sub(sector_return, axis=0)
    return result


def _inverse_sector_revision_breadth(
    revision: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Inverse same-direction sector revision breadth, bounded for stability."""
    labels = sector.reindex(index=revision.index, columns=revision.columns).ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=revision.index, columns=revision.columns)
    direction = np.sign(revision)

    for label in labels.dropna().unique():
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        group_direction = direction.loc[:, columns]
        valid = group_direction.notna()
        positive_share = group_direction.gt(0.0).sum(axis=1).div(valid.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan))
        negative_share = group_direction.lt(0.0).sum(axis=1).div(valid.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan))
        same_direction = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(
                group_direction.gt(0.0),
                np.asarray(positive_share)[:, None],
                np.where(group_direction.lt(0.0), np.asarray(negative_share)[:, None], np.nan),
            ),
            index=revision.index,
            columns=columns,
        )
        result.loc[:, columns] = 1.0 - same_direction.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    return result.fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticRevisionPassThroughDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks isolated EPS-consensus revisions not confirmed by sector-relative returns."""

    factor_id = "idiosyncratic_revision_pass_through_deficit"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Revision Pass-Through Deficit"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Sector-normalized quarterly-scale EPS-estimate revisions less recent "
        "sector-relative price performance, amplified when same-direction "
        "sector revision breadth is low."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ["close", "epsEstimate", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        prior_estimate = estimate.shift(63)
        revision = (estimate - prior_estimate).div(prior_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revision = revision.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        normalized_revision = _sector_zscore(revision, sector).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        relative_price = _sector_relative_return(returns(data), sector, 21).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        breadth_deficit = _inverse_sector_revision_breadth(revision, sector)

        pass_through_deficit = (normalized_revision - relative_price) * breadth_deficit
        signal = rank(pass_through_deficit.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""Investors often reward reported per-share earnings growth without immediately separating operating profit growth from mechanically lower share counts. The signal identifies firms whose EPS growth materially exceeds net-income growth while buybacks coincide with weak free-cash-flow support and rising debt, a combination consistent with financial engineering rather than improving economics. The edge should be falsified if these firms do not subsequently underperform otherwise comparable firms after the disclosure becomes incorporated; the natural opposite side is headline-oriented earnings and buyback demand."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _valid_accounting_mask(
    eps_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    income_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    shares_growth: pd.DataFrame,
    free_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Require contemporaneously available, economically plausible inputs."""
    finite = (
        np.isfinite(eps_growth)
        & np.isfinite(income_growth)
        & np.isfinite(shares_growth)
        & np.isfinite(free_cash_flow)
        & np.isfinite(debt_growth)
    )
    plausible_growth = (
        eps_growth.abs().le(10.0)
        & income_growth.abs().le(10.0)
        & shares_growth.abs().le(5.0)
        & debt_growth.abs().le(10.0)
    )
    return finite & plausible_growth


@register_factor
class BuybackFinancedEpsQualityUnwind(BaseFactor):
    """Short debt-financed buyback-driven EPS growth unsupported by cash flow."""

    factor_id = "buyback_financed_eps_quality_unwind"
    name = "Debt-Financed EPS Engineering Unwind"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional score for firms where EPS growth exceeds net "
        "income growth while share count contracts, free cash flow is weak, and "
        "debt is increasing; these characteristics indicate potentially fragile "
        "buyback-financed EPS engineering."
    )
    window_length = 1
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsGrowth",
        "netIncomeGrowth",
        "sharesGrowth",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "debtGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_growth = data["epsGrowth"]
        income_growth = data["netIncomeGrowth"]
        shares_growth = data["sharesGrowth"]
        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]
        debt_growth = data["debtGrowth"]

        valid = _valid_accounting_mask(
            eps_growth,
            income_growth,
            shares_growth,
            free_cash_flow,
            debt_growth,
        )

        # EPS growth above aggregate earnings growth is the per-share accounting wedge.
        eps_wedge = (eps_growth - income_growth).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        # Negative share growth denotes a shrinking denominator from repurchases.
        buyback_intensity = (-shares_growth).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        # Rank FCF within each disclosure cross-section: weak/negative FCF is risky.
        fcf_rank = rank(free_cash_flow.where(valid))
        weak_fcf = 1.0 - fcf_rank

        # Positive debt growth provides the financing channel.
        debt_financing = debt_growth.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        wedge_rank = rank(eps_wedge.where(valid))
        buyback_rank = rank(buyback_intensity.where(valid))
        debt_rank = rank(debt_financing.where(valid))

        engineering_strength = (
            wedge_rank.fillna(0.0)
            * buyback_rank.fillna(0.0)
            * weak_fcf.fillna(0.0)
            * debt_rank.fillna(0.0)
        )

        # High engineering strength is expected to unwind, hence the negative sign.
        signal = -rank(engineering_strength.where(valid))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""Revenue-consensus revisions are usually processed faster than the full earnings implication, especially for firms with high fixed operating-cost intensity where a sales revision has convex consequences for margins and EPS. Go long firms with favorable revenue-estimate acceleration whose EPS consensus has not yet caught up, and short the opposite configuration. The mechanism is falsified if subsequent EPS-estimate changes do not close the revenue-to-EPS revision gap; slow analyst-model updates and investors' focus on top-line headlines are the expected source of delay."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _revision_acceleration(estimate: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, scale-normalised difference between fast and slow estimate revisions."""
    level = estimate.astype(float)
    prior_level = level.shift(1)

    # A rolling absolute-level median makes EPS revisions comparable even for
    # loss-making firms, where percentage changes around zero are unstable.
    level_scale = (
        level.abs()
        .rolling(126, min_periods=20)
        .median()
        .replace(0.0, np.nan)
    )
    innovation = (level - prior_level) / level_scale
    innovation = innovation.where(level.notna() & prior_level.notna(), 0.0)
    innovation = innovation.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    innovation = innovation.clip(-5.0, 5.0)

    # Estimate fields are quarterly step functions.  These two exponentially
    # decayed revision kernels retain a recent filing/revision event while
    # removing the mechanically repeated daily estimate level.
    fast = innovation.ewm(halflife=4, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()
    slow = innovation.ewm(halflife=30, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

    # Normalise by the name's own trailing revision-event magnitude, rather
    # than by the dispersion of the step-function level itself.
    revision_rms = np.sqrt(
        innovation.pow(2).rolling(252, min_periods=40).mean()
    ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    acceleration = (fast - slow) / revision_rms
    return acceleration.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-8.0, 8.0)


def _operating_leverage_weight(
    sga_to_revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    rd_to_revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_margin: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct a bounded fixed-cost absorption proxy from reported ratios."""
    fixed_cost_intensity = (
        sga_to_revenue.astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        + rd_to_revenue.astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    ).clip(upper=2.0)

    # A given revenue surprise has greater earnings sensitivity when fixed
    # costs are material relative to a thin operating-profit cushion.
    margin_cushion = operating_margin.astype(float).abs().clip(lower=0.03)
    leverage_proxy = (fixed_cost_intensity / margin_cushion).clip(0.0, 20.0)
    return leverage_proxy.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class OperatingLeverageRevisionTransmission(BaseFactor):
    """Revenue-to-EPS estimate-revision gap amplified by operating leverage."""

    factor_id = "operating_leverage_revision_transmission"
    name = "Operating-Leverage Revision Transmission"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional sector-neutral rank of a recent revenue-consensus "
        "revision acceleration minus the slower EPS-consensus response, scaled "
        "by fixed-cost operating-leverage intensity."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsEstimate",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "rdToRevenue",
        "operatingMargin",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(template)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(template)

        revenue_acceleration = _revision_acceleration(revenue_estimate)
        eps_acceleration = _revision_acceleration(eps_estimate)

        # Positive values identify a fresh favourable top-line revision whose
        # implied EPS revision has not yet been incorporated into consensus.
        revision_gap = revenue_acceleration - eps_acceleration
        leverage_proxy = _operating_leverage_weight(
            data["sgaToRevenue"].reindex_like(template),
            data["rdToRevenue"].reindex_like(template),
            data["operatingMargin"].reindex_like(template),
        )
        leverage_weight = (0.5 + rank(leverage_proxy).fillna(0.5)).clip(0.5, 1.5)
        transmitted_gap = (revision_gap * leverage_weight).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        sector = data["sector"].reindex_like(template).fillna("Unknown")
        sector_neutral_gap = indneutralize(transmitted_gap, sector)
        return rank(sector_neutral_gap).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.0)

"""Information often arrives through economically connected peer groups, while individual names adjust with heterogeneous speed because of liquidity, analyst coverage, and investor attention. Build a rolling return-correlation graph and isolate coherent peer-mode moves rather than treating a sector average as the relevant benchmark; buy stocks lagging a broad positive mode and short stocks lagging a broad negative mode. The hypothesis is falsified when coherent graph-mode moves do not predict catch-up returns after excluding the stock's own contribution, while the opposite side is supplied by traders treating the move as idiosyncratic noise or by constrained relative-value capital."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import linalg

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _spectral_peer_lag_signal(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 60,
    short_window: int = 3,
    n_modes: int = 3,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally extract broad non-market correlation modes and peer residuals."""
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    n_time, n_assets = close_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_time, n_assets), np.nan, dtype=float)

    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ret_values = close_values[1:] / close_values[:-1] - 1.0
    ret_values = np.vstack((np.full((1, n_assets), np.nan), ret_values))
    ret_values[~np.isfinite(ret_values)] = np.nan
    ret_values = np.clip(ret_values, -0.75, 0.75)

    ret = pd.DataFrame(ret_values, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    short_return = ret.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).sum().to_numpy()

    min_observations = max(20, int(np.ceil(0.85 * lookback)))
    sqrt_short = np.sqrt(float(short_window))

    for t in range(lookback - 1, n_time):
        trailing = ret_values[t - lookback + 1 : t + 1]
        finite = np.isfinite(trailing)
        counts = finite.sum(axis=0)

        means = np.divide(
            np.nansum(trailing, axis=0),
            counts,
            out=np.full(n_assets, np.nan),
            where=counts > 0,
        )
        centered = np.where(finite, trailing - means[None, :], 0.0)
        sum_squares = np.sum(centered * centered, axis=0)
        volatility = np.sqrt(
            np.divide(
                sum_squares,
                np.maximum(counts - 1, 1),
                out=np.full(n_assets, np.nan),
                where=counts > 1,
            )
        )

        standardized_move = short_return[t] / (volatility * sqrt_short)
        valid = (
            (counts >= min_observations)
            & np.isfinite(volatility)
            & (volatility > 1e-8)
            & np.isfinite(standardized_move)
        )
        asset_index = np.flatnonzero(valid)
        k = len(asset_index)
        if k < max(6, n_modes + 2):
            continue

        x = centered[:, asset_index]
        ss = np.sum(x * x, axis=0)
        denominator = np.sqrt(np.outer(ss, ss))
        correlation = np.divide(
            x.T @ x,
            denominator,
            out=np.zeros((k, k), dtype=float),
            where=denominator > 1e-12,
        )
        correlation = np.clip(correlation, -1.0, 1.0)
        np.fill_diagonal(correlation, 1.0)

        # Fixed diagonal shrinkage stabilizes noisy daily peer graphs while
        # retaining the eigenvectors of genuinely coherent return clusters.
        shrinkage = 0.20
        correlation = (1.0 - shrinkage) * correlation + shrinkage * np.eye(k)

        extract = min(n_modes + 1, k)
        try:
            eigenvalues, eigenvectors = linalg.eigh(
                correlation,
                subset_by_index=(k - extract, k - 1),
                check_finite=False,
            )
        except (ValueError, np.linalg.LinAlgError):
            continue

        # The largest eigenpair is the market-like graph mode.  The remaining
        # leading modes capture peer structures not explained by that broad move.
        mode_values = eigenvalues[:-1][::-1]
        mode_vectors = eigenvectors[:, :-1][:, ::-1]
        if mode_values.size == 0:
            continue

        effective_members = 1.0 / np.sum(mode_vectors**4, axis=0)
        broad_threshold = max(5.0, 0.12 * k)
        broad = effective_members >= broad_threshold
        excess_correlation = np.maximum(mode_values - 1.0, 0.0)
        weights = excess_correlation * np.minimum(
            1.0, effective_members / max(0.25 * k, 1.0)
        )
        weights = np.where(broad & (mode_values > 1.05), weights, 0.0)
        total_weight = float(np.sum(np.abs(weights)))
        if total_weight <= 1e-12:
            continue

        move = standardized_move[asset_index]
        mode_scores = mode_vectors.T @ move

        # For each eigenmode, remove stock i's own projection before forming
        # its peer-implied move.  This is the leave-one-out catch-up benchmark.
        own_loading_sq = mode_vectors * mode_vectors
        peer_denominator = np.maximum(1.0 - own_loading_sq, 1e-6)
        peer_components = mode_vectors * (
            mode_scores[None, :] - mode_vectors * move[:, None]
        ) / peer_denominator
        peer_move = (peer_components * weights[None, :]).sum(axis=1) / total_weight

        residual_lag = peer_move - move
        output[t, asset_index] = np.clip(residual_lag, -10.0, 10.0)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class SpectralPeerModeLagAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    """Peer-mode residual lag signal from a rolling spectral return graph."""

    factor_id = "spectral_peer_mode_lag_assimilation"
    name = "Spectral Peer-Mode Lag Assimilation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "From trailing daily returns, construct a shrinkage correlation graph and "
        "extract broad non-market spectral modes. For each stock, calculate a "
        "leave-one-out peer-implied recent return from mode loadings, subtract its "
        "realized return, and rank the resulting catch-up residual."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        signal = _spectral_peer_lag_signal(data["close"])
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.0)

programs.code:
"""The CAPE-style mechanism in value_matters_predictability_of_stock_index_returns implies that valuation is a slow-moving return anchor while momentum captures the short-run path by which prices move toward or away from that anchor. Stocks that are cheap relative to sector peers and already beginning to outperform are more likely experiencing gradual belief updating toward fundamentals; richly valued names that are starting to underperform face the symmetric unwind. The signal should fail if the conditional continuation of value-aligned trends is no stronger than either standalone value or standalone momentum, indicating that the apparent anchor is not economically relevant at the six-bar horizon."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_relative_momentum(close: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal 20-to-40-bar momentum phase, neutralized against sector peers.

    The short 20-bar return identifies the current price phase, while the
    40-bar return anchors that phase in a slower trend.  Averaging their
    sector-relative ranks reduces broad sector-cycle exposure without using
    future observations.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    momentum_20 = safe_close / safe_close.shift(20) - 1.0
    momentum_40 = safe_close / safe_close.shift(40) - 1.0

    rel_20 = indneutralize(momentum_20, sector)
    rel_40 = indneutralize(momentum_40, sector)
    return 0.5 * (rank(rel_20) + rank(rel_40)) - 0.5


def _sector_value_anchor(
    earnings_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    pe_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct a sector-relative, positive-earnings valuation anchor.

    Earnings yield is preferred where reported and positive.  A positive PE
    inverse supplies a point-in-time fallback.  Loss-making and unavailable
    observations remain masked rather than being treated as cheap.
    """
    positive_yield = earnings_yield.where(earnings_yield > 0.0)
    positive_pe_inverse = (1.0 / pe_ratio.where(pe_ratio > 0.0)).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )
    value = positive_yield.combine_first(positive_pe_inverse)
    relative_value = indneutralize(value, sector)
    return rank(relative_value) - 0.5

class ValuationAnchorPhaseAlignment(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral value anchors reinforced only by aligned price momentum."""

    factor_id = "valuation_anchor_phase_alignment"
    name = "Valuation Anchor Phase Alignment"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral positive earnings-yield valuation rank combined with "
        "sector-relative 20-to-40-bar price momentum; rewards cheap stocks "

    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "earningsYield", "peRatio", "sector"]

        close = data["close"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        earnings_yield = data["earningsYield"]
        pe_ratio = data["peRatio"]

        value_anchor = _sector_value_anchor(earnings_yield, pe_ratio, sector)
        momentum_phase = _sector_relative_momentum(close, sector)

        # Agreement is multiplicative: a strong value anchor only receives a
        # high score when the price path points toward it.  The additive term

"""Analysts and investors frequently process an EPS-consensus revision as a headline event, but the persistence of that revision depends on whether it is supported by revenue expectations and improving operating leverage. A positive EPS-estimate change accompanied by positive revenue-estimate change and rising operating or gross margins is more likely an information-rich profitability update than a transient accounting effect, yet constrained attention can delay full repricing. The hypothesis is falsified if price-adjusted, operating-confirmed revisions do not outperform unconfirmed revisions or if their effect is fully incorporated on the update date."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _decayed_report_state(
    event_values: pd.DataFrame,
    event_mask: pd.DataFrame,
    decay: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry report-date shocks forward with an exponentially decaying state.

    The recursion is causal: row t depends only on its report event and the
    state already available at t - 1.  A new report replaces the prior state,
    which avoids treating a quarterly step function as a sequence of daily
    revisions.
    """
    values = event_values.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    mask = event_mask.fillna(False).to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    state = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)

    for row in range(values.shape[0]):
        if row > 0:
            state[row] = decay * state[row - 1]
        if mask[row].any():
            state[row, mask[row]] = values[row, mask[row]]

    return pd.DataFrame(state, index=event_values.index, columns=event_values.columns)


def _relative_report_revision(
    estimates: pd.DataFrame, floor: float, decay: float) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Extract a bounded revision only when a point-in-time estimate changes."""
    previous = estimates.shift(1)
    valid = estimates.notna() & previous.notna()
    changed = valid & estimates.ne(previous)
    denominator = previous.abs().clip(lower=floor)
    revision = ((estimates - previous) / denominator).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
    state = _decayed_report_state(revision.where(changed, 0.0), changed, decay)
    activity = _decayed_report_state(changed.astype(float), changed, decay)
    return state, activity


def _margin_change_state(margin: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the decayed report-to-report change in a profitability margin."""
    previous = margin.shift(1)
    changed = margin.notna() & previous.notna() & margin.ne(previous)
    change = (margin - previous).clip(-0.50, 0.50)
    return _decayed_report_state(change.where(changed, 0.0), changed, decay)


def _price_response_since_update(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    update_mask: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally measure price movement from the latest estimate-update date."""
    anchor = close.where(update_mask).ffill()
    response = close / anchor.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    return response.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class OperatingLeverageRevisionUnderreaction(BaseFactor):
    """Price-adjusted analyst revisions confirmed by revenue and margin improvement."""

    factor_id = "operating_leverage_revision_underreaction"
    name = "Operating-Leverage Confirmed Revision Lag"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks recent EPS-consensus revisions that are corroborated by revenue "
        "estimate revisions and improving operating or gross margins, after "
        "subtracting the price response since the latest estimate update."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingMargin",
        "grossMargin",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        gross_margin = data["grossMargin"]

        # Quarterly estimate fields are step functions.  Only actual step
        # changes are treated as information events; the state then decays over
        # roughly one trading month while attention gradually incorporates it.
        decay = float(np.exp(-1.0 / 21.0))
        eps_revision, eps_activity = _relative_report_revision(
            eps_estimate, 0.05, decay
        )
        revenue_revision, revenue_activity = _relative_report_revision(
            revenue_estimate, 1.0, decay
        )

        operating_change = _margin_change_state(operating_margin, decay)
        gross_change = _margin_change_state(gross_margin, decay)
        margin_support = 0.65 * operating_change + 0.35 * gross_change

        # Revenue agreement and operating-leverage improvement increase the
        # credibility of either an upward or downward EPS revision symmetrically.
        base_revision = 0.70 * eps_revision + 0.30 * revenue_revision
        revenue_confirmation = np.tanh(4.0 * revenue_revision)
        margin_confirmation = np.tanh(8.0 * margin_support)
        confirmed_revision = base_revision * (
            1.0 + 0.35 * revenue_confirmation + 0.45 * margin_confirmation
        )

        update_mask = (
            (eps_activity > 0.95)
            | (revenue_activity > 0.95)
        )
        price_response = _price_response_since_update(close, update_mask)

        # The price adjustment is itself decayed, so an old report does not
        # dominate the cross-section after the revision information has expired.
        recency = np.maximum(eps_activity, revenue_activity)
        unabsorbed_revision = confirmed_revision - price_response * recency
        unabsorbed_revision = unabsorbed_revision.replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        return rank(unabsorbed_revision).fillna(0.0)

"""Repurchases are not uniformly good news: a buyback funded from operating cash flow by a cheaply valued firm can return surplus capital, while a debt-funded buyback at an expensive valuation can be a fragile attempt to support per-share metrics. Investors often react to the gross repurchase announcement or reported share-count reduction before disentangling funding source and valuation discipline. The trade should be rejected if debt-financed and cash-financed repurchases have indistinguishable subsequent cross-sectional returns after controlling for valuation and sector.

Mechanism: identify firms whose reported repurchases are plausibly financed from
internally generated cash, penalize concurrent debt funding and deteriorating
coverage, then interact the capital-allocation signal with sector-relative value.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _safe_ratio(numerator: pd.DataFrame, denominator: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a finite ratio while preserving unavailable observations as NaN."""
    denom = denominator.where(denominator.abs() > 1.0e-12)
    result = numerator / denom
    return result.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _quarterly_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, lag: int = 63) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal slow change suitable for point-in-time quarterly step functions."""
    return frame - frame.shift(lag)


@register_factor
class CashFinancedBuybackValueRelease(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative value signal conditioned on cash-financed repurchase quality."""

    factor_id = "cash_financed_buyback_value_release"
    name = "Cash-Financed Buyback Value Release"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Long cheaply valued firms whose reported repurchases are covered by "
        "operating cash generation and not accompanied by debt funding; short "
        "expensive firms with debt-supported repurchases and worsening coverage."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "shareRepurchase",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "freeCashFlow",
        "netDebtIssuance",
        "debtGrowth",
        "interestCoverage",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "earningsYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]

        repurchase = (-data["shareRepurchase"]).clip(lower=0.0)
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        free_cash_flow = data["freeCashFlow"]
        net_debt_issuance = data["netDebtIssuance"]
        debt_growth = data["debtGrowth"]
        coverage = data["interestCoverage"]

        # Internal funding is strongest when buybacks are covered by both OCF
        # and FCF.  Negative FCF cannot finance a distribution sustainably.
        ocf_coverage = _safe_ratio(repurchase, operating_cash_flow.clip(lower=0.0))
        fcf_coverage = _safe_ratio(repurchase, free_cash_flow.clip(lower=0.0))
        cash_funded = 1.0 - 0.5 * ocf_coverage.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        cash_funded -= 0.5 * fcf_coverage.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        # Positive debt issuance concurrent with distributions, rising leverage,
        # and falling interest coverage indicate financially fragile buybacks.
        debt_funding = _safe_ratio(net_debt_issuance.clip(lower=0.0), repurchase)
        debt_funding = debt_funding.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        leverage_penalty = debt_growth.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        coverage_change = _quarterly_change(coverage)
        coverage_deterioration = _safe_ratio(
            (-coverage_change).clip(lower=0.0), coverage.abs() + 1.0
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        buyback_active = repurchase.gt(0.0).astype(float)
        allocation_quality = buyback_active * (
            cash_funded.fillna(-1.0)
            - debt_funding.fillna(1.0)
            - 0.5 * leverage_penalty
            - 0.5 * coverage_deterioration.fillna(0.0)
        )

        # Sector demeaned value prevents the signal from becoming a persistent
        # industry bet between structurally high- and low-yield sectors.
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        earnings_yield = data["earningsYield"].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        value = 0.5 * fcf_yield.fillna(0.0) + 0.5 * earnings_yield.fillna(0.0)
        sector_value = indneutralize(value, data["sector"])

        quality_score = rank(allocation_quality)
        value_score = rank(sector_value)
        signal = (quality_score - 0.5) * (value_score - 0.5)

        return rank(signal).reindex(index=template.index, columns=template.columns)

"""A positive EPS surprise generated alongside a revenue beat and improving operating profitability is more likely to reflect durable demand and operating leverage than one generated solely by temporary cost cutting. Market participants often trade the reported earnings headline before separating top-line strength from margin quality, leaving a short post-report repricing window. The hypothesis is falsified if revenue-plus-margin-confirmed surprises do not outperform equally sized EPS-only surprises over the following week."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify point-in-time step-function updates using only current/prior bars."""
    previous = frame.shift(1)
    return frame.notna() & (previous.isna() | frame.ne(previous))


def _report_to_report_change(
    frame: pd.DataFrame, report_event: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Hold the latest causal quarter-over-quarter change between report dates."""
    reported_value = frame.where(report_event & frame.notna())
    prior_reported_value = reported_value.ffill().shift(1)
    change_at_report = (frame - prior_reported_value).where(
        report_event & frame.notna()
    )
    return change_at_report.ffill()


def _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally standardize with a MAD scale and standard-dev fallback."""
    median = frame.median(axis=1)
    centered = frame.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad_scale = centered.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    std_scale = frame.std(axis=1, ddof=0)
    scale = mad_scale.where(mad_scale > 1.0e-12, std_scale)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 1.0e-12)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class ToplineMarginSurpriseDurability(BaseFactor):
    """Confirmed revenue, earnings, and margin surprises identify durable post-report drift."""

    factor_id = "topline_margin_surprise_durability"
    name = "Top-Line and Margin Surprise Durability"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "At newly available reports, rewards only EPS and revenue surprises "
        "whose directions agree with quarter-over-quarter operating- and "
        "gross-margin changes; contradictory components receive a neutral score."
    )
    window_length = 260
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "operatingMargin",
        "grossMargin",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        gross_margin = data["grossMargin"]

        eps_update = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_update = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        operating_update = _update_mask(operating_margin)
        gross_update = _update_mask(gross_margin)
        report_event = eps_update | revenue_update | operating_update | gross_update

        operating_qoq = _report_to_report_change(operating_margin, report_event)
        gross_qoq = _report_to_report_change(gross_margin, report_event)

        eps_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        operating_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(operating_qoq)
        gross_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(gross_qoq)

        all_positive = (
            (eps_z > 0.0)
            & (revenue_z > 0.0)
            & (operating_z > 0.0)
            & (gross_z > 0.0)
        )
        all_negative = (
            (eps_z < 0.0)
            & (revenue_z < 0.0)
            & (operating_z < 0.0)
            & (gross_z < 0.0)
        )
        aligned = all_positive | all_negative

        composite = (eps_z + revenue_z + operating_z + gross_z) / 4.0
        signal = composite.where(aligned & report_event, 0.0)
        return signal.fillna(0.0).astype(float).reindex_like(template)

"""Analysts and discretionary investors often process EPS and revenue misses using familiar templates, but jointly unusual earnings reports that are far from a firm's own historical EPS-revenue surprise pattern require slower model and narrative revision. Go long firms with recently released, coherent positive EPS-and-revenue surprises that are statistically off their historical surprise manifold, and short analogous negative ruptures. The mechanism is falsified if manifold-distance conditioning adds no incremental post-release return predictability beyond the signed EPS and revenue surprises themselves; it may persist because rare multi-dimensional outcomes are difficult to assimilate into standardized analyst models and institutional earnings workflows within several trading days."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _trailing_event_moments(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum_events: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return strictly prior trailing event mean and variance.

    ``values`` is sparse except at report events.  Calendar-time rolling
    windows therefore retain the last several quarterly observations without
    treating forward-filled daily copies as independent observations.
    """
    mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)
    second = (
        values.pow(2)
        .rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events)
        .mean()
        .shift(1)
    )
    variance = (second - mean.pow(2)).clip(lower=1.0e-8)
    return mean, variance


def _historical_covariance(
    x: pd.DataFrame,
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum_events: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute prior event-distribution moments for a two-dimensional panel."""
    mean_x = x.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)
    mean_y = y.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)
    second_x = x.pow(2).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)
    second_y = y.pow(2).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)
    cross = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_events).mean().shift(1)

    var_x = (second_x - mean_x.pow(2)).clip(lower=1.0e-6)
    var_y = (second_y - mean_y.pow(2)).clip(lower=1.0e-6)
    covariance = cross - mean_x * mean_y
    return mean_x, mean_y, var_x, var_y, covariance


def _decayed_event_signal(
    event_signal: pd.DataFrame,
    valid_event: pd.DataFrame,
    decay_bars: float,
    maximum_age: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Forward carry a report signal causally, with exponential event aging."""
    n_rows, n_cols = event_signal.shape
    row_number = np.arange(n_rows, dtype=float)[:, None]
    event_rows = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(valid_event.to_numpy(), row_number, np.nan),
        index=event_signal.index,
        columns=event_signal.columns,
    )
    last_event_row = event_rows.ffill()
    age = pd.DataFrame(
        row_number - last_event_row.to_numpy(),
        index=event_signal.index,
        columns=event_signal.columns,
    )
    carried = event_signal.where(valid_event).ffill()
    decay = np.exp(-age / decay_bars)
    return (carried * decay).where(age.le(maximum_age))


@register_factor
class JointSurpriseManifoldRuptureDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Rank coherent earnings-report surprises by their historical manifold rupture."""

    factor_id = "joint_surprise_manifold_rupture_drift"
    name = "Joint Surprise Manifold Rupture Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "At a newly available report, standardize EPS and revenue surprises "
        "against prior report events, measure their causal two-dimensional "
        "Mahalanobis novelty, and decay coherent signed ruptures after release."
    )
    window_length = 1260
    inputs = ["close", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "epsActual", "revenueActual"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close)

        available = eps_surprise.notna() & revenue_surprise.notna()
        changed_surprise = (
            eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
            | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        changed_actual = (
            eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
            | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        )
        report_event = available & (changed_surprise | changed_actual)

        eps_event = eps_surprise.where(report_event)
        revenue_event = revenue_surprise.where(report_event)

        raw_eps_mean, raw_eps_var = _trailing_event_moments(eps_event, 1260, 6)
        raw_revenue_mean, raw_revenue_var = _trailing_event_moments(
            revenue_event, 1260, 6
        )

        z_eps = (eps_surprise - raw_eps_mean) / np.sqrt(raw_eps_var)
        z_revenue = (revenue_surprise - raw_revenue_mean) / np.sqrt(raw_revenue_var)
        z_eps_event = z_eps.where(report_event)
        z_revenue_event = z_revenue.where(report_event)

        mean_x, mean_y, var_x, var_y, covariance = _historical_covariance(
            z_eps_event, z_revenue_event, 1260, 6
        )
        dx = z_eps - mean_x
        dy = z_revenue - mean_y
        correlation = (covariance / np.sqrt(var_x * var_y)).clip(-0.95, 0.95)
        denominator = (1.0 - correlation.pow(2)).clip(lower=0.05)
        mahalanobis_sq = (
            dx.pow(2) / var_x
            - 2.0 * correlation * dx * dy / np.sqrt(var_x * var_y)
            + dy.pow(2) / var_y
        ) / denominator
        novelty = np.sqrt(mahalanobis_sq.clip(lower=0.0))

        same_direction = (z_eps * z_revenue).gt(0.0)
        joint_magnitude = 0.5 * (z_eps.abs() + z_revenue.abs())
        signed_joint = np.sign(z_eps + z_revenue) * joint_magnitude
        rupture = (signed_joint * novelty).where(same_direction & report_event)

        valid_event = report_event & rupture.notna() & np.isfinite(rupture)
        decayed = _decayed_event_signal(
            rupture, valid_event, decay_bars=6.0, maximum_age=18
        )
        return rank(decayed).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: Analysts and discretionary investors often process EPS and revenue misses using familiar templates, but jointly unusual earnings reports that are far from a firm's own historical EPS-revenue surprise pattern require slower model and narrative revision. Go long firms with recently released, coherent positive EPS-and-revenue surprises that are statistically off their historical surprise manifold, and short analogous negative ruptures. The mechanism is falsified if manifold-distance conditioning adds no incremental post-release return predictability beyond the signed EPS and revenue surprises themselves; it may persist because rare multi-dimensional outcomes are difficult to assimilate into standardized analyst models and institutional earnings workflows within several trading days.

The score is the signed, same-direction joint surprise magnitude multiplied by this novelty distance and decayed from the report date over subsequent bars, then cross-sectionally ranked.

"""A large sector-wide return shock is not incorporated simultaneously across names: lower-turnover firms can lag the sector move because informed and index-arbitrage capital concentrates first in liquid bellwethers. The trade buys financially resilient underreactors after positive sector shocks and shorts resilient overreactors, with signs reversed following negative shocks; resilience controls reduce the chance that a lag reflects genuinely different distress exposure. The other side is liquidity-constrained investors and passive benchmark traders who transmit sector information unevenly, and the idea fails if idiosyncratic residual returns contain no subsequent convergence toward sector-implied returns."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_equal_weight_returns(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map each stock to its contemporaneous static-sector equal-weight return."""
    labels = sector.iloc[0].reindex(stock_returns.columns).astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__MISSING_SECTOR__")

    sector_panel = stock_returns.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).mean().T
    mapped = sector_panel.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy()).copy()
    mapped.columns = stock_returns.columns
    return mapped


def _rolling_beta(
    y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing OLS beta of y on x, computed panelwise."""
    mean_y = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_x = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    covariance = (y * x).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean() - mean_y * mean_x
    variance_x = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean() - mean_x * mean_x
    return covariance / variance_x.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _clean_fundamental(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove non-finite point-in-time fundamental observations."""
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SectorShockResilienceAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-shock underreaction signal gated by liquidity and balance-sheet resilience."""

    factor_id = "sector_shock_resilience_assimilation"
    name = "Sector Shock Resilience Assimilation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Estimates trailing stock sensitivity to equal-weight sector returns and "
        "trades the signed beta-adjusted return gap after unusually large sector "
        "shocks, only when current relative turnover is subdued and balance-sheet "
        "resilience is above median."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "cashRatio",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)

        stock_return = close / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        stock_return = stock_return.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_return = _sector_equal_weight_returns(stock_return, data["sector"])

        # Estimate sensitivity only with information known before today's shock.
        beta = _rolling_beta(stock_return, sector_return, 60).shift(1)
        beta = beta.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        residual = stock_return - beta * sector_return
        residual_volatility = residual.rolling(40, min_periods=30).std().shift(1)
        residual_gap = residual / residual_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # The sector shock is standardized using volatility observed through t-1.
        sector_volatility = sector_return.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        standardized_shock = sector_return / sector_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        shock_gate = ((standardized_shock.abs() - 1.25) / 2.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        shock_sign = np.sign(standardized_shock)

        # Below-normal turnover identifies names in which assimilation is likeliest delayed.
        normal_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        relative_volume = volume / normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        liquidity_gate = (1.0 - relative_volume).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        cash_rank = rank(_clean_fundamental(data["cashRatio"]))
        current_rank = rank(_clean_fundamental(data["currentRatio"]))
        leverage_rank = rank(-_clean_fundamental(data["debtToEquity"]))
        coverage_rank = rank(_clean_fundamental(data["interestCoverage"]))
        resilience = (
            cash_rank.fillna(0.5)
            + current_rank.fillna(0.5)
            + leverage_rank.fillna(0.5)
            + coverage_rank.fillna(0.5)
        ) / 4.0
        resilience_gate = ((resilience - 0.50) / 0.50).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # Positive shocks favor negative residual gaps; negative shocks favor positive gaps.
        raw_signal = (
            -shock_sign
            * residual_gap
            * shock_gate
            * liquidity_gate
            * resilience_gate
        )
        eligible = (
            (shock_gate > 0.0)
            & (liquidity_gate > 0.0)
            & (resilience_gate > 0.0)
            & raw_signal.notna()
        )

        ranked_signal = (rank(raw_signal.where(eligible)) - 0.5) * 2.0
        return ranked_signal.fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""A sharp down move accompanied by abnormal volume and a close near the bar low is more likely to continue when the issuer has weak near-term liquidity and heavy refinancing dependence. Such firms face a sparse-liquidity constraint: risk limits, margin calls, ETF redemptions, and constrained dealer balance sheets can force sales before fundamental investors can absorb supply. The signal is falsified if stressed balance-sheet names show the same or lower conditional continuation than cash-rich peers after otherwise comparable price-volume shocks."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _downside_flow_intensity(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 60,
    half_life: float = 3.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal Hawkes-style intensity of clustered downside volume shocks."""
    ret = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
    ret_mean = ret.rolling(lookback, min_periods=20).mean()
    ret_std = ret.rolling(lookback, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downside_z = ((ret - ret_mean) / ret_std).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)

    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0))
    vol_mean = log_volume.rolling(lookback, min_periods=20).mean()
    vol_std = log_volume.rolling(lookback, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    volume_z = ((log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)

    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.5)
    low_close_pressure = 1.0 - close_location

    event = (
        (-downside_z).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        * volume_z.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        * low_close_pressure
    )

    decay = float(np.exp(-np.log(2.0) / half_life))
    values = event.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=True)
    intensity = np.zeros_like(values)
    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        if t == 0:
            intensity[t] = values[t]
        else:
            intensity[t] = decay * intensity[t - 1] + values[t]

    intensity_df = pd.DataFrame(intensity, index=event.index, columns=event.columns)
    prior_pressure = decay * intensity_df.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    return event * (1.0 + prior_pressure)


def _rollover_vulnerability(
    short_term_debt: pd.DataFrame,
    current_liabilities: pd.DataFrame,
    cash: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    interest_coverage: pd.DataFrame,
    net_debt_to_ebitda: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional composite of near-term refinancing and liquidity weakness."""
    safe_cash = cash.where(cash > 0.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    debt_to_cash = (short_term_debt / safe_cash).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    liabilities_to_cash = (current_liabilities / safe_cash).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    debt_to_cash = debt_to_cash.clip(lower=0.0, upper=100.0)
    liabilities_to_cash = liabilities_to_cash.clip(lower=0.0, upper=100.0)

    weak_current_ratio = -current_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=20.0)
    weak_coverage = -interest_coverage.clip(lower=-100.0, upper=100.0)
    levered_balance_sheet = net_debt_to_ebitda.clip(lower=0.0, upper=100.0)

    components = [
        rank(debt_to_cash),
        rank(liabilities_to_cash),
        rank(weak_current_ratio),
        rank(weak_coverage),
        rank(levered_balance_sheet),
    ]

    numerator = sum(component.fillna(0.0) for component in components)
    denominator = sum(component.notna().astype(float) for component in components)
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class RolloverStressFlowCascade(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral short signal for self-reinforcing forced-selling pressure."""

    factor_id = "rollover_stress_flow_cascade"
    name = "Rollover Stress Flow Cascade"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks clustered downside price-volume shocks more highly when weak cash "
        "coverage, near-term liabilities, poor liquidity ratios, weak interest "
        "coverage, and leverage imply refinancing stress; the final score is "
        "sector-neutralized for short-cascade selection."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "shortTermDebt",
        "totalCurrentLiabilities",
        "cash",
        "currentRatio",
        "interestCoverage",
        "netDebtToEbitda",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        flow_cascade = _downside_flow_intensity(
            data["close"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        vulnerability = _rollover_vulnerability(
            data["shortTermDebt"],
            data["totalCurrentLiabilities"],
            data["cash"],
            data["currentRatio"],
            data["interestCoverage"],
            data["netDebtToEbitda"],
        )

        raw_score = flow_cascade * (0.25 + vulnerability)
        cross_sectional_score = rank(raw_score).fillna(0.5)
        sectors = data["sector"].fillna("Unknown")
        return indneutralize(cross_sectional_score, sectors).fillna(0.0)

"""When daily returns become unusually synchronized across the market, a common risk shock dominates firm-specific price discovery and capital reallocates toward balance-sheet quality. In that state, profitable cash-rich firms with conservative leverage should outperform fragile firms over the following week because passive de-risking and mandate-constrained investors cannot immediately rebalance every exposure. This is a cross-sectional implementation of factor timing: it should fail if high return synchrony does not raise the subsequent quality-minus-fragility spread, despite the signal being active only during common-shock regimes.

Mechanism: elevated same-direction participation and a high trailing first-PC
share identify common-shock regimes; the factor activates a defensive quality
portfolio only when idiosyncratic price discovery is suppressed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _market_synchrony(ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal common-shock intensity from directional breadth and PC variance.

    Directional synchrony is the absolute cross-sectional mean of return signs.
    The PCA component is computed from the trailing pairwise correlation matrix:
    its largest eigenvalue divided by the trace is the fraction of standardized
    return variation explained by the common component.  Each row uses only the
    preceding ``window`` observations, including the current bar.
    """
    index = ret.index
    columns = ret.columns
    values = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape

    direction = np.sign(values)
    direction[~np.isfinite(direction)] = np.nan
    valid_counts = np.sum(np.isfinite(direction), axis=1)
    directional = np.abs(np.nansum(direction, axis=1)) / np.where(
        valid_counts > 0, valid_counts, np.nan
    )

    pc_share = np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float)
    min_assets = 3
    for end in range(window - 1, n_rows):
        sample = values[end - window + 1 : end + 1]
        available = np.sum(np.isfinite(sample), axis=0) >= max(5, window // 2)
        if int(available.sum()) < min_assets:
            continue

        x = sample[:, available]
        medians = np.nanmedian(x, axis=0)
        x = np.where(np.isfinite(x), x, medians)
        x = x - np.mean(x, axis=0, keepdims=True)
        scales = np.std(x, axis=0, ddof=1)
        keep = np.isfinite(scales) & (scales > 1.0e-12)
        if int(keep.sum()) < min_assets:
            continue

        z = x[:, keep] / scales[keep]
        corr = np.dot(z.T, z) / max(window - 1, 1)
        corr = (corr + corr.T) * 0.5
        try:
            largest = float(np.linalg.eigvalsh(corr)[-1])
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue
        trace = float(np.trace(corr))
        if trace > 0.0 and np.isfinite(largest):
            pc_share[end] = largest / trace

    raw = 0.5 * directional + 0.5 * pc_share
    raw_frame = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(raw[:, None], n_cols, axis=1), index=index, columns=columns
    )
    baseline = raw_frame.rolling(60, min_periods=20).mean()
    dispersion = raw_frame.rolling(60, min_periods=20).std()
    zscore = (raw_frame - baseline) / dispersion.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return zscore.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0) / 3.0


def _quality_composite(
    roe: pd.DataFrame,
    roic: pd.DataFrame,
    gross_margin: pd.DataFrame,
    fcf_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_assets: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional defensive quality score with robust sparse-data handling."""
    profitability = (
        rank(roe.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0))
        + rank(roic.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0))
        + rank(gross_margin.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0))
    ) / 3.0
    liquidity = (
        rank(fcf_yield.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0))
        + rank(cash_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=20.0))
    ) / 2.0
    leverage_defense = (
        1.0 - rank(debt_to_equity.clip(lower=-5.0, upper=20.0))
        + 1.0 - rank(debt_to_assets.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0))
    ) / 2.0

    score = 0.45 * profitability + 0.25 * liquidity + 0.30 * leverage_defense
    return (score - 0.5).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class SynchronyGatedQualityDefense(BaseFactor):
    """Defensive quality ranking activated only in common-shock regimes."""

    factor_id = "synchrony_gated_quality_defense"
    name = "Common-Shock Quality Defense"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Measure causal market synchrony from same-direction breadth and the "
        "trailing first-principal-component share of return variation. During "
        "elevated synchrony, rank profitable, cash-rich, conservatively "
        "levered firms and shrink the score toward zero otherwise."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "roe",
        "roic",
        "grossMargin",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "debtToAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        ret = returns(data).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        synchrony = _market_synchrony(ret, 20)

        quality = _quality_composite(
            data["roe"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["roic"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["grossMargin"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["freeCashFlowYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["debtToEquity"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
            data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
        )

        signal = quality * synchrony
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
