"""Stress-conditioned stale-surprise relay.

Mechanism: broad industry drawdowns make investors reallocate toward firms whose
new earnings information demonstrates balance-sheet resilience, while negative
news from financially fragile firms can accelerate the common shock."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(labels: pd.DataFrame, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """Extract stable classification labels for cross-sectional grouping."""
    return labels.iloc[0].reindex(columns).fillna("__unknown__").astype(str)


def _group_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile rank separately within each static classification group."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    groups = labels.reindex(clean.columns).fillna("__unknown__").astype(str)
    return clean.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T


def _estimate_age(
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame, revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal number of bars since either available consensus series changed."""
    eps = eps_estimate.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    revenue = revenue_estimate.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rows, cols = eps.shape
    age = np.full((rows, cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    previous_eps = np.full(cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
    previous_revenue = np.full(cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
    previous_active = np.zeros(cols, dtype=bool)

    for t in range(rows):
        current_eps = eps[t]
        current_revenue = revenue[t]
        active = np.isfinite(current_eps) | np.isfinite(current_revenue)
        changed_eps = np.isfinite(current_eps) & (
            ~np.isfinite(previous_eps)
            | (np.abs(current_eps - previous_eps) > 1e-12)
        )
        changed_revenue = np.isfinite(current_revenue) & (
            ~np.isfinite(previous_revenue)
            | (np.abs(current_revenue - previous_revenue) > 1e-12)
        )
        changed = active & (changed_eps | changed_revenue)

        if t == 0:
            age[t, active] = 0.0
        else:
            continuing = active & previous_active & ~changed
            age[t, continuing] = age[t - 1, continuing] + 1.0
            age[t, active & ~continuing] = 0.0

        previous_eps = current_eps.copy()
        previous_revenue = current_revenue.copy()
        previous_active = active

    return pd.DataFrame(age, index=eps_estimate.index, columns=eps_estimate.columns)


def _report_update_mask(
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify point-in-time earnings report arrivals from step-function changes."""
    actual_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
        eps_actual.shift(1).isna()
        | (np.abs(eps_actual - eps_actual.shift(1)) > 1e-12)
    )
    surprise_changed = eps_surprise.notna() & (
        eps_surprise.shift(1).isna()
        | (np.abs(eps_surprise - eps_surprise.shift(1)) > 1e-12)
    )
    return actual_changed | surprise_changed


def _leave_one_out_downside(
    close: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broad, volatility-scaled peer drawdown excluding the stock itself."""
    ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    move = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    valid = move.notna().astype(float)
    values = move.fillna(0.0)
    groups = industry.reindex(close.columns).fillna("__unknown__").astype(str)

    total = values.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    count = valid.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    peer_count = count - valid
    peer_move = (total - values).div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    negative = (move < 0.0).astype(float).where(move.notna(), 0.0)
    negative_total = negative.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("sum").T
    negative_share = (negative_total - negative).div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    peer_vol = peer_move.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    standardized = peer_move.div(peer_vol).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    broadness = ((negative_share - 0.50) / 0.50).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return (-standardized).clip(lower=0.0) * broadness


@register_factor
class StressedStaleSurpriseBalanceSheetRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks earnings-news propagation through industry stress and financial buffers."""

    factor_id = "stressed_stale_surprise_balance_sheet_relay"
    name = "Stressed Stale-Surprise Balance-Sheet Relay"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Carries stale-consensus EPS surprise events for six bars and activates "
        "them during broad leave-one-out industry drawdowns, favoring resilient "
        "positive-surprise firms and fragile negative-surprise firms."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "totalAssets",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        sector = _static_labels(data["sector"], close.columns)
        industry = _static_labels(data["industry"], close.columns)

        assets = data["totalAssets"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cash_flow_assets = data["operatingCashFlow"].div(assets)
        absorption_parts = [
            _group_rank(data["cashRatio"], sector),
            1.0 - _group_rank(data["debtToEquity"], sector),
            _group_rank(cash_flow_assets, sector),
            _group_rank(data["incomeQuality"], sector),
        ]
        absorption = sum(absorption_parts) / float(len(absorption_parts))

        update = _report_update_mask(data["epsActual"], data["epsSurprise"])
        age = _estimate_age(data["epsEstimate"], data["revenueEstimate"])
        stale_weight = (age / 63.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        estimate_scale = data["epsEstimate"].abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].div(estimate_scale).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        signed_surprise = 2.0 * _group_rank(relative_surprise, sector) - 1.0

        positive_state = absorption
        negative_state = 1.0 - absorption
        directional_state = positive_state.where(signed_surprise >= 0.0, negative_state)
        event_impulse = (signed_surprise * directional_state * (0.25 + 0.75 * stale_weight)).where(update)

        relay_memory = event_impulse.fillna(0.0).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum()
        industry_stress = _leave_one_out_downside(close, industry)
        raw = relay_memory * industry_stress
        active = industry_stress.notna() & relay_memory.ne(0.0) & absorption.notna()

        return _group_rank(raw, sector).where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Stressed Stale-Surprise Balance-Sheet Relay
programs.trading_idea: A stale-consensus earnings surprise becomes more informative when a broad industry drawdown forces investors to discriminate rapidly between firms that can absorb funding and demand shocks and firms that cannot. During peer stress, positive surprises from liquid, cash-generative firms signal resilient earnings capacity and attract defensive rotation, while negative surprises from fragile firms reveal that the industry shock is likely to propagate through financing constraints. Neither parent alone identifies this news-by-stress transmission channel: the surprise lacks a systemic allocation state, while balance-sheet quality lacks a fresh catalyst that reveals which firms are actually diverging.
programs.description: The factor carries a six-bar memory of stale-consensus EPS-surprise events, scales positive news by sector-relative financial absorption and negative news by fragility, and activates the signal only during broad leave-one-out industry drawdowns. It then ranks the conditional relay signal within sectors.

programs.code:
"""Industry breadth relay conditioned on stale firm-specific information.

Mechanism: coherent flow across several close industry peers is a proxy for a
portfolio-level demand wave rather than a single-name event.  A firm whose last
earnings release is no longer fresh has less idiosyncratic public information to
resist that wave, making it susceptible to delayed cross-excitation of investor
attention and institutional execution.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _exp_memory(events: pd.DataFrame, half_life: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponential marked-event memory with unit impact at an event."""
    values = events.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    out = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)
    decay = float(np.exp(-np.log(2.0) / half_life))
    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        if t == 0:
            out[t] = values[t]
        else:
            out[t] = decay * out[t - 1] + values[t]
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)


def _leave_one_out_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels_frame: pd.DataFrame, minimum_group: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Static-label leave-one-out group mean, evaluated independently each day."""
    labels = labels_frame.iloc[0].astype(object).fillna("__unknown_group__")
    array = values.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    out = np.zeros_like(array, dtype=float)
    label_values = labels.to_numpy()

    for group in pd.unique(labels):
        loc = np.flatnonzero(label_values == group)
        if len(loc) < minimum_group:
            continue
        group_values = array[:, loc]
        group_sum = np.sum(group_values, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        out[:, loc] = (group_sum - group_values) / float(len(loc) - 1)

    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)


def _sector_demean(signal: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove daily sector-common demand, retaining within-sector relay effects."""
    labels = sector.iloc[0].astype(object).fillna("__unknown_sector__")
    array = signal.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    out = np.zeros_like(array, dtype=float)
    label_values = labels.to_numpy()

    for group in pd.unique(labels):
        loc = np.flatnonzero(label_values == group)
        if len(loc) < 3:
            continue
        group_values = array[:, loc]
        out[:, loc] = group_values - np.mean(group_values, axis=1, keepdims=True)

    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=signal.index, columns=signal.columns)


def _earnings_freshness(
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Infer report arrivals from point-in-time quarterly-field changes.

    A new available report resets freshness to one; otherwise freshness decays
    causally.  The validity mask prevents missing fundamental histories from
    being interpreted as stale information.
    """
    eps = eps_actual.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    revenue = revenue_actual.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = eps.notna() | revenue.notna()
    prior_valid = valid.shift(1).fillna(False)

    eps_changed = eps.notna() & eps.shift(1).notna() & eps.ne(eps.shift(1))
    revenue_changed = (
        revenue.notna()
        & revenue.shift(1).notna()
        & revenue.ne(revenue.shift(1))
    )
    arrival = valid & ((~prior_valid) | eps_changed | revenue_changed)
    freshness = _exp_memory(arrival.astype(float), 18.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    return freshness, valid.astype(float)


@register_factor
class IndustryBreadthStaleInformationRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "industry_breadth_stale_information_relay"
    name = "Industry Breadth Stale-Information Relay"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-wide coherent signed-flow pressure, gated by breadth and by "
        "the age of a firm's last earnings disclosure. Long stale-information "
        "laggards behind positive peer flow and short analogous negative-flow names."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        volatility = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_ret = (ret / volatility).clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)
        average_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = (volume / average_volume).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        marks = (np.tanh(standardized_ret) * participation).fillna(0.0)

        # Signed pressure is the own-flow state.  A separate bounded sign mark
        # measures whether peer pressure is broad rather than concentrated.
        own_pressure = _exp_memory(marks, 4.0)
        active_signed = np.sign(marks).where(marks.abs() >= 0.50, 0.0)
        peer_breadth_pressure = _leave_one_out_mean(
            _exp_memory(active_signed, 3.0), data["industry"], 4
        )

        # Large absolute group-average signed activity requires several peers to
        # align; a single extreme constituent is diluted by the group average.
        breadth_gate = np.tanh(peer_breadth_pressure.abs() / 0.35)
        peer_lag = peer_breadth_pressure - own_pressure

        freshness, fundamental_valid = _earnings_freshness(
            data["epsActual"], data["revenueActual"]
        )
        information_staleness = (1.0 - freshness).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        raw_signal = peer_lag * breadth_gate * information_staleness * fundamental_valid
        idiosyncratic_signal = _sector_demean(raw_signal, data["sector"])
        signal = rank(idiosyncratic_signal) - 0.5
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry Breadth Stale-Information Relay
programs.trading_idea: Broad, same-direction flow across economically close industry peers is more likely to represent a distributed institutional theme than a single-stock shock. Firms without a recent earnings disclosure have less firm-specific information to counteract that thematic demand, so they are more susceptible to delayed cross-excitation and should catch up in the peer-flow direction. The edge persists because portfolio-manager rebalancing, differentiated liquidity, and slow fundamental-information processing distribute thematic orders across constituents over several sessions; it is falsified if broad peer flow has no incremental six-bar predictive power among firms with stale earnings information after sector demeaning.
programs.description: Computes exponentially decayed signed-flow pressure and requires it to be broad and directionally coherent across leave-one-out industry peers. It buys stale-information firms lagging positive broad peer flow and shorts stale-information firms lagging negative broad peer flow, while removing sector-common effects.

programs.code:
"""Revision drift confirmed by absorbed directional institutional flow.

Mechanism: concurrent EPS and revenue revisions identify a broad update to the
firm's outlook.  A revision is most likely still underpriced when clustered
abnormal trading agrees with its direction but has generated unusually little
price impact, indicating that dealer inventory is absorbing an unfinished
informed order rather than that the news has already cleared the market.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _changed_with_history(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a public update only when adjacent observations are available."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    prior = clean.shift(1)
    return clean.notna() & prior.notna() & clean.ne(prior)


def _absorbed_flow_confirmation(
    close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame, revision: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal signed-flow confirmation with a stock-specific impact deficit."""
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    safe_volume = volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    volume_base = safe_volume.ewm(halflife=20, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    abnormal_volume = np.log(safe_volume / volume_base).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    mark = np.sign(ret.fillna(0.0)) * abnormal_volume.fillna(0.0)

    signed_flow = mark.ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
    absolute_flow = mark.abs().ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
    background_flow = mark.abs().ewm(halflife=20, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    directional_balance = signed_flow / absolute_flow.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    excitation = absolute_flow / background_flow.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    recent_impact = ret.abs().rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum() / abnormal_volume.rolling(
        3, min_periods=3
    ).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normal_impact = ret.abs().rolling(20, min_periods=12).sum() / abnormal_volume.rolling(
        20, min_periods=12
    ).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    impact_deficit = (normal_impact / recent_impact.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
        lower=0.25, upper=4.0
    )

    flow_strength = np.log1p(excitation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)) * impact_deficit
    concordant = (np.sign(revision) * directional_balance) > 0.0
    return revision * flow_strength.where(concordant, 0.0)


@register_factor
class RevisionAbsorptionConcordanceDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "revision_absorption_concordance_drift"
    name = "Revision-Absorption Concordance Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks concurrent EPS and revenue consensus revisions only when their "
        "direction is confirmed by clustered abnormal volume with a muted "
        "stock-specific price impact."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        eps = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(template).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(template).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(template)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(template)

        eps_prior = eps.shift(1)
        revenue_prior = revenue.shift(1)
        eps_change = ((eps - eps_prior) / eps_prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
            lower=-2.0, upper=2.0
        )
        revenue_change = (
            (revenue - revenue_prior) / revenue_prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)

        concurrent = _changed_with_history(eps) & _changed_with_history(revenue)
        same_direction = (eps_change * revenue_change) > 0.0
        report_rollover = _changed_with_history(eps_surprise) | _changed_with_history(
            revenue_surprise
        )
        valid_revision = concurrent & same_direction & ~report_rollover
        revision = (0.5 * eps_change + 0.5 * revenue_change).where(valid_revision, 0.0)

        raw = _absorbed_flow_confirmation(data["close"], data["volume"], revision)
        return rank(raw).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Revision-Absorption Concordance Drift
programs.trading_idea: A simultaneous EPS-and-revenue revision is more credible when the market is already exhibiting unusually clustered directional trading consistent with the revision, but that flow has not yet generated its normal price impact. The estimate change supplies the fundamental information direction, while muted-impact metaorder flow identifies an implementation and inventory-absorption state in which that information is still being accumulated rather than fully incorporated into price. Neither parent alone distinguishes informed revisions from weak consensus noise or directional flow from non-informational execution; their concordance isolates revisions being validated by unfinished institutional demand.
programs.description: The signal retains aligned EPS and revenue consensus revisions only when they agree with a recent, abnormal, same-signed volume-flow cluster whose realized price impact is below the stock's normal impact. It cross-sectionally ranks the signed revision weighted by the strength of this absorbed-flow confirmation.

programs.code:
"""Cash-gated alignment of quiet attention with impact absorption states.

Mechanism: signed abnormal volume with compressed intrabar range can indicate an
unfinished execution program.  Its predictive direction is amplified only when
cash-quality revisions and changing sell-pressure impact jointly validate either
liquidity absorption with improving fundamentals or adverse distribution with
deteriorating fundamentals.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_residual(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove static sector-wide activity from each cross-section."""
    labels_frame = sector.reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labels = labels_frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0].fillna("Unknown")
    sector_mean = values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return values - sector_mean


def _attention_conversion(
    attention: pd.DataFrame,
    price_impulse: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing partial excitation coefficient controlling price-event memory."""
    attention_state = attention.ewm(alpha=0.15, adjust=False).mean().shift(1)
    price_state = price_impulse.ewm(alpha=0.15, adjust=False).mean().shift(1)

    mean_a = attention_state.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_p = price_state.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    mean_y = price_impulse.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()

    var_a = (
        attention_state.mul(attention_state).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_a.mul(mean_a)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    var_p = (
        price_state.mul(price_state).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_p.mul(mean_p)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    cov_ap = (
        attention_state.mul(price_state).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_a.mul(mean_p)
    )
    cov_ay = (
        attention_state.mul(price_impulse).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_a.mul(mean_y)
    )
    cov_py = (
        price_state.mul(price_impulse).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_p.mul(mean_y)
    )

    determinant = var_a.mul(var_p) - cov_ap.mul(cov_ap)
    ridge = 0.05 * var_a.mul(var_p)
    beta = (cov_ay.mul(var_p) - cov_py.mul(cov_ap)).div(
        (determinant + ridge).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    )

    var_y = (
        price_impulse.mul(price_impulse).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
        - mean_y.mul(mean_y)
    ).clip(lower=0.0)
    strength = cov_ay.abs().div(np.sqrt(var_a.mul(var_y)).replace(0.0, np.nan))
    return beta.mul(strength.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _cash_quality_revision(
    income_quality: pd.DataFrame,
    operating_cash_flow_growth: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Public-information cash realization revision using a quarterly lag."""
    quality = income_quality.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cash_growth = operating_cash_flow_growth.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    quality_change = (quality - quality.shift(21)).where(
        quality.notna() & quality.shift(21).notna()
    )
    growth_change = (cash_growth - cash_growth.shift(21)).where(
        cash_growth.notna() & cash_growth.shift(21).notna()
    )
    return 0.65 * (2.0 * rank(quality_change) - 1.0).fillna(0.0) + 0.35 * (
        2.0 * rank(growth_change) - 1.0
    ).fillna(0.0)


def _impact_release(
    open_price: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Positive when persistent sell pressure is causing less marginal damage."""
    safe_open = open_price.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    bar_range = (high - low).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downside = ((open_price - close).clip(lower=0.0) / safe_open).clip(upper=0.50)

    volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_volume = (volume / volume_base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 4.0)
    range_fraction = ((open_price - close).clip(lower=0.0) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    pressure = (range_fraction * relative_volume).where(lambda x: x > 0.0)
    impact = (downside / pressure).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    recent = impact.rolling(4, min_periods=2).mean()
    earlier = impact.shift(4).rolling(8, min_periods=4).mean()
    release = (earlier - recent).div(earlier.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    active_pressure = pressure.fillna(0.0).rolling(3, min_periods=1).mean()
    return (release * active_pressure).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class CashGatedAttentionConversionAlignment(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_gated_attention_conversion_alignment"
    name = "Cash-Gated Attention Conversion Alignment"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks signed quiet-volume attention times its trailing attention-to-price "
        "conversion coefficient, with exposure increased when that direction agrees "
        "with cash-quality-conditioned sell-impact release."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "incomeQuality",
        "operatingCashFlowGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        high = data["high"].where(data["high"] > 0.0)
        low = data["low"].where(data["low"] > 0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        bar_range = (high - low).abs().div(close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_base = bar_range.rolling(19, min_periods=10).median()
        range_ratio = bar_range.div(range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 10.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume)
        vol_mean = log_volume.rolling(41, min_periods=20).mean()
        vol_std = log_volume.rolling(39, min_periods=20).std()
        abnormal_volume = log_volume.sub(vol_mean).div(vol_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 5.0)

        raw_span = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (2.0 * close.sub(low).div(raw_span) - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        direction = 0.5 * np.sign(ret.fillna(0.0)) + 0.5 * close_location
        quietness = 1.0 / (1.0 + range_ratio.fillna(1.0))
        attention = abnormal_volume * quietness * direction

        return_vol = ret.rolling(21, min_periods=10).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        return_shock = ret.abs().div(return_vol).clip(0.0, 5.0)
        price_impulse = (
            np.sign(ret.fillna(0.0))
            * return_shock.fillna(0.0)
            * range_ratio.fillna(0.0).clip(upper=3.0)
            * close_location.abs()
            * (1.0 + abnormal_volume)
        )

        attention_idio = _sector_residual(attention.fillna(0.0), data["sector"])
        impulse_idio = _sector_residual(price_impulse.fillna(0.0), data["sector"])
        conversion = _attention_conversion(attention_idio, impulse_idio, 80)
        converted_attention = (attention_idio * conversion).clip(-10.0, 10.0)

        impact_state = _impact_release(
            data["open"].fillna(0.0),
            data["high"].fillna(0.0),
            data["low"].fillna(0.0),
            data["close"].fillna(0.0),
            volume,
        )
        cash_revision = _cash_quality_revision(
            data["incomeQuality"], data["operatingCashFlowGrowth"]
        )
        validation_state = impact_state * (0.5 + 0.5 * cash_revision.abs())
        aligned = (converted_attention * validation_state) > 0.0
        gate = 0.25 + 0.75 * aligned.astype(float)
        signal = (converted_attention * gate).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Cash-Gated Attention Conversion Alignment
programs.trading_idea: Quiet abnormal volume can reveal an unfinished institutional execution schedule, but its direction is most credible when liquidity-impact curvature and recently disclosed cash-quality revisions identify whether liquidity suppliers are absorbing flow or withdrawing from it. The factor estimates each name's historical conversion of signed quiet attention into price impulses, then increases exposure only when the current latent attention direction agrees with the cash-quality-conditioned impact state. This interaction separates informed accumulation or absorbed liquidation from mechanically similar but fundamentally unsupported volume bursts, which neither attention conversion nor cash-gated impact release can identify alone.
programs.description: Computes sector-residual signed low-range abnormal-volume attention and a trailing partial conversion coefficient into price impulses. It gates that converted attention by the directional agreement between cash-quality-conditioned sell-impact release and the current attention-conversion signal.

programs.code:
"""Sector-residual reversal after systemic liquidity recovery.

Mechanism: a broad simultaneous range-and-volume shock signals a market-wide
liquidity withdrawal.  If a stock's own activity compresses on the following
bar while its sector-relative displacement remains large, the original move is
more likely completed forced flow than continuing private-information arrival;
dealer inventory normalization should reverse the residual displacement.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_residual(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract each ticker's contemporaneous sector median causally.

    Sector labels are static metadata.  Missing labels are assigned unique
    groups so that unknown names are not spuriously pooled together.
    """
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0].copy()
    fallback = pd.Series(
        ["__unknown_" + str(column) for column in values.columns],
        index=values.columns,
        dtype=object,
    )
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), fallback).astype(str)
    sector_median = values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("median").T
    return values - sector_median


def _systemic_shock_gate(joint_stress: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Lagged abnormal breadth of joint range-volume stress, broadcast by name.

    The baseline uses only observations through t-1.  The returned gate is
    additionally lagged because this factor trades the recovery phase after a
    synchronized shock rather than the shock bar itself.
    """
    breadth = joint_stress.gt(np.log(1.35)).where(joint_stress.notna()).mean(axis=1)
    center = breadth.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).median()
    scale = breadth.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).std()
    surprise = ((breadth - center) / (scale + 0.03)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
    lagged = surprise.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(lagged.to_numpy()[:, None], joint_stress.shape[1], axis=1),
        index=joint_stress.index,
        columns=joint_stress.columns,
    )


@register_factor
class SystemicLiquidityRecoveryResidualReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "systemic_liquidity_recovery_residual_reversal"
    name = "Systemic Liquidity Recovery Residual Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades a sector-residual two-day displacement only after a lagged "
        "synchronized liquidity shock and subsequent name-level activity "
        "normalization, targeting completed forced-flow impact."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].ffill()
        high = data["high"].where(data["high"].notna(), close)
        low = data["low"].where(data["low"].notna(), close)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        relative_range = ((high - low).abs() / previous_close).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        range_base = relative_range.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).median()
        volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).median()
        range_abnormality = np.log(
            relative_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        volume_abnormality = np.log(
            volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        joint_stress = np.minimum(range_abnormality, volume_abnormality)

        systemic_gate = _systemic_shock_gate(joint_stress)
        prior_name_stress = joint_stress.shift(1).fillna(0.0)

        volume_compression = (
            1.0 - volume / volume.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        range_compression = (
            1.0 - relative_range / relative_range.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        recovery = np.sqrt(volume_compression * range_compression).fillna(0.0)

        residual_ret = _sector_residual(ret, data["sector"])
        residual_displacement = residual_ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum()
        signal = -residual_displacement * prior_name_stress * recovery * systemic_gate

        return rank(signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.5)

"""Earnings-shock propagation conditional on opposing liquidity-driven flow.

Mechanism: a coherent, unusual earnings surprise is a common information shock,
but persistent high-participation order flow in the opposite direction can reflect
liquidity-constrained rebalancing and delayed information assimilation.  The
factor trades in the fundamental-surprise direction only when that opposing flow
remains directionally self-exciting.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _exp_intensity(events: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed marked-event intensity."""
    values = np.nan_to_num(events.to_numpy(dtype=float), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    output = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)
    if len(values) > 0:
        output[0] = values[0]
        for row in range(1, len(values)):
            output[row] = values[row] + decay * output[row - 1]
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)

def _carry_event_state(event_state: pd.DataFrame, valid_event: pd.DataFrame, decay_bars: float, maximum_age: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Forward-carry an event state with causal age-based exponential decay."""
    n_rows = event_state.shape[0]
    rows = np.arange(n_rows, dtype=float)[:, None]
    event_rows = pd.DataFrame(np.where(valid_event.to_numpy(), rows, np.nan), index=event_state.index, columns=event_state.columns)
    last_row = event_rows.ffill()
    age = pd.DataFrame(rows - last_row.to_numpy(), index=event_state.index, columns=event_state.columns)
    carried = event_state.where(valid_event).ffill()
    decay = np.exp(-age / decay_bars)
    return (carried * decay).where(age.le(maximum_age))

def _prior_event_scale(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strictly-prior robust scale of sparse quarterly event observations."""
    return values.abs().rolling(757, min_periods=4).median().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

@register_factor
class SurpriseRuptureOpposingFlowRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'surprise_rupture_opposing_flow_release_j'
    name = 'Surprise-Rupture Opposing-Flow Release'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Trades coherent, own-history-unusual EPS and revenue surprises only when a persistent high-volume order-flow cascade runs in the opposite direction, indicating delayed information propagation through constrained liquidity.'
    window_length = 756
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'epsSurprise', 'revenueSurprise', 'epsActual', 'revenueActual']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].ffill()
        volume = data['volume'].reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        eps = data['epsSurprise'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue = data['revenueSurprise'].reindex_like(close)
        eps_actual = data['epsActual'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_actual = data['revenueActual'].reindex_like(close)
        available = eps.notna() & revenue.notna()
        changed = eps.ne(eps.shift(1)) | revenue.ne(revenue.shift(1)) | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)) | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        report_event = available & changed
        eps_event = eps.where(report_event)
        revenue_event = revenue.where(report_event)
        eps_scale = _prior_event_scale(eps_event)
        revenue_scale = _prior_event_scale(revenue_event)
        z_eps = (eps / eps_scale).clip(lower=-8.0, upper=8.0)
        z_revenue = (revenue / revenue_scale).clip(lower=-8.0, upper=8.0)
        coherent = (z_eps * z_revenue).gt(0.0)
        joint_size = np.sqrt((z_eps.abs() * z_revenue.abs()).clip(lower=0.0))
        rupture = (np.sign(z_eps + z_revenue) * joint_size).where(report_event & coherent)
        valid_rupture = report_event & rupture.notna() & np.isfinite(rupture)
        surprise_state = _carry_event_state(rupture, valid_rupture, decay_bars=8.0, maximum_age=18).fillna(0.0)
        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        vol_median = volume.rolling(42, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vol_tail = volume.rolling(43, min_periods=20).quantile(0.8)
        mark = (volume / vol_median - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        tail = (volume >= vol_tail) & vol_tail.notna()
        buy_events = mark.where(tail & ret.gt(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        sell_events = mark.where(tail & ret.lt(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        decay = float(np.exp(-1.0 / 6.0))
        buy_intensity = _exp_intensity(buy_events, decay)
        sell_intensity = _exp_intensity(sell_events, decay)
        total_intensity = buy_intensity + sell_intensity
        directional_flow = (buy_intensity - sell_intensity) / (total_intensity + 1e-08)
        directional_persistence = directional_flow.abs()
        state_sign = np.sign(surprise_state)
        opposing_flow = (-state_sign * directional_flow).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        signal = state_sign * surprise_state.abs().clip(upper=8.0) * opposing_flow * directional_persistence * np.log1p(total_intensity)
        return rank(signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.5)

Such opposing flow is consistent with liquidity-constrained rebalancing, stale-position unwinds, or slow institutional model revision absorbing the shock rather than disproving it. The interaction has edge neither parent has alone: surprise novelty identifies when a flow imbalance is informative rather than generic, while persistent opposite-signed flow identifies delayed shock propagation rather than an already-completed earnings drift.

"""Public earnings ruptures with absorbed crowding predict short-horizon reversal.

Mechanism: a coherent earnings and revenue surprise makes subsequent directional
volume highly visible and reactive.  When that flow accelerates but its price
impact remains muted, passive liquidity is absorbing a crowded post-news
rebalance; unlike an unobserved parent order, this publicly induced pressure is
more likely to unwind over the next several sessions.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _carry_rupture_state(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Create a causal, decaying state for coherent report surprises."""
    available = eps_surprise.notna() & revenue_surprise.notna()
    changed = (
        eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
    )
    event = available & changed

    eps_event = eps_surprise.where(event)
    revenue_event = revenue_surprise.where(event)
    lookback = 1260
    eps_mean = eps_event.rolling(lookback, min_periods=5).mean().shift(1)
    rev_mean = revenue_event.rolling(lookback, min_periods=5).mean().shift(1)
    eps_std = eps_event.rolling(lookback, min_periods=5).std().shift(1)
    rev_std = revenue_event.rolling(lookback, min_periods=5).std().shift(1)

    z_eps = ((eps_surprise - eps_mean) / eps_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
    z_rev = ((revenue_surprise - rev_mean) / rev_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
    coherent = (z_eps * z_rev).gt(0.0)

    # The weaker channel determines confidence: a large EPS surprise alone is
    # not enough to call this a broad fundamental rupture.
    strength = np.sign(z_eps + z_rev) * np.minimum(z_eps.abs(), z_rev.abs())
    rupture = strength.where(event & coherent & strength.abs().ge(0.5))
    valid = rupture.notna() & np.isfinite(rupture)

    rows = np.arange(len(rupture.index), dtype=float)[:, None]
    event_rows = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(valid.to_numpy(), rows, np.nan),
        index=rupture.index,
        columns=rupture.columns,
    )
    last_row = event_rows.ffill()
    age = pd.DataFrame(
        rows - last_row.to_numpy(),
        index=rupture.index,
        columns=rupture.columns,
    )
    carried = rupture.where(valid).ffill()
    state = carried * np.exp(-age / 7.0)
    return state.where(age.le(12.0)), age


def _hawkes_absorption_pressure(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return signed fresh arrival pressure and a trailing muted-impact weight."""
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))
    volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

    prior_vol = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    typical_volume = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    rel_volume = volume.div(typical_volume).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)

    active = ret.abs().div(prior_vol).ge(0.25) & rel_volume.ge(1.0)
    mark = np.log1p(rel_volume.clip(upper=8.0)).where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    buy = mark.where(ret.gt(0.0), 0.0)
    sell = mark.where(ret.lt(0.0), 0.0)

    decay = float(np.exp(-1.0 / 3.0))
    buy_intensity = buy.ewm(alpha=1.0 - decay, adjust=False).mean()
    sell_intensity = sell.ewm(alpha=1.0 - decay, adjust=False).mean()
    total = buy_intensity + sell_intensity
    imbalance = (buy_intensity - sell_intensity).div(total.replace(0.0, np.nan))

    signed_intensity = buy_intensity - sell_intensity
    fresh_acceleration = (
        signed_intensity.ewm(alpha=0.50, adjust=False).mean()
        - signed_intensity.ewm(alpha=0.15, adjust=False).mean()
    )
    fresh_direction = np.sign(fresh_acceleration).where(fresh_acceleration.abs().gt(0.01), 0.0)
    cluster = 1.0 - np.exp(-total.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0))
    pressure = imbalance * cluster * fresh_direction

    displacement = ret.rolling(4, min_periods=4).sum().abs().div(
        (prior_vol * np.sqrt(4.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    )
    muted = np.exp(-displacement.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0))
    return pressure, muted


@register_factor
class EarningsRuptureAbsorptionCrowdingReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "earnings_rupture_absorption_crowding_reversal"
    name = "Rupture Absorption Crowding Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks surprise-aligned, accelerating signed-volume clusters whose "
        "post-news price displacement remains muted, identifying absorbed "
        "crowding expected to reverse over six bars."
    )
    window_length = 1260
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        state, age = _carry_rupture_state(
            data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["epsActual"].reindex_like(close),
            data["revenueActual"].reindex_like(close),
        )
        pressure, muted = _hawkes_absorption_pressure(
            close,
            data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close),
        )

        aligned = (state * pressure).gt(0.0)
        post_report = age.ge(1.0) & age.le(10.0)
        severity = state.abs().clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        raw = (np.sign(state) * pressure.abs() * muted * severity).where(
            aligned & post_report
        )
        sector_relative = indneutralize(raw, data["sector"])
        return rank(sector_relative).fillna(0.5).reindex(
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _market_panel(series: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    values = np.repeat(series.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(values, index=series.index, columns=columns)


def _conditional_corr(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    market_ret: pd.Series,
    event: pd.Series,
    window: int,
    min_events: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    market = _market_panel(market_ret, stock_ret.columns)
    event_panel = _market_panel(event.astype(float), stock_ret.columns).gt(0.0)
    valid = stock_ret.notna() & market.notna() & event_panel
    weight = valid.astype(float)
    x = market.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    y = stock_ret.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    count = weight.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    safe_count = count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    sx = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sy = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    syy = (y * y).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    vx = sxx / safe_count - (sx / safe_count) ** 2
    vy = syy / safe_count - (sy / safe_count) ** 2
    cov = sxy / safe_count - (sx / safe_count) * (sy / safe_count)
    denom = np.sqrt(vx.clip(lower=0.0) * vy.clip(lower=0.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cov / denom).where(count >= float(min_events)).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)


def _downside_semibeta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    market_ret: pd.Series,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    market = _market_panel(market_ret, stock_ret.columns)
    valid = stock_ret.notna() & market.lt(0.0)
    x = market.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    y = stock_ret.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    numerator = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=50).sum()
    denominator = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=50).sum()
    return numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _cross_sectional_residual(target: pd.DataFrame, control: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid = target.notna() & control.notna()
    weight = valid.astype(float)
    count = weight.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    y = target.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    x = control.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    mean_y = y.sum(axis=1) / count
    mean_x = x.sum(axis=1) / count
    dy = y.sub(mean_y, axis=0).where(valid, 0.0)
    dx = x.sub(mean_x, axis=0).where(valid, 0.0)
    slope = (dx * dy).sum(axis=1) / (dx * dx).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    fitted = pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(mean_y.to_numpy()[:, None], target.shape[1], axis=1),
        index=target.index,
        columns=target.columns,
    ).add(control.sub(mean_x, axis=0).mul(slope, axis=0))
    return (target - fitted).where(valid & (count >= 8.0))


def _fear_activation(market_ret: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    downside_sq = market_ret.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2)
    recent = downside_sq.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean().pow(0.5)
    baseline = downside_sq.shift(5).rolling(63, min_periods=40).mean().pow(0.5)
    down_days = market_ret.lt(0.0).astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    active = recent.gt(baseline) & down_days.ge(3.0) & baseline.gt(0.0)
    intensity = (recent / baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
    return intensity.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class FearTailVisibilityRotation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fear_tail_visibility_rotation"
    name = "Fear Tail-Visibility Rotation"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "In persistent fear regimes, buy already-capitulated high-semibeta names "
        "and short resilient apparent shelters with semibeta-unexplained increases "
        "in downside-tail dependence."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        stock_ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.50, 0.50)
        market_ret = stock_ret.median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)

        semibeta = _downside_semibeta(stock_ret, market_ret, 126)
        sector_semibeta = indneutralize(semibeta.clip(-3.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0), data["sector"])
        visible_risk = rank(sector_semibeta).sub(0.5).fillna(0.0)

        tail_cutoff = market_ret.rolling(126, min_periods=80).quantile(0.20)
        downside_tail = market_ret.le(tail_cutoff) & market_ret.lt(0.0)
        tail_recent = _conditional_corr(stock_ret, market_ret, downside_tail, 42, 6)
        tail_base = _conditional_corr(stock_ret, market_ret, downside_tail, 126, 18)
        all_days = pd.Series(True, index=close.index)
        ordinary_recent = _conditional_corr(stock_ret, market_ret, all_days, 42, 24)
        ordinary_base = _conditional_corr(stock_ret, market_ret, all_days, 126, 80)
        tail_innovation = (tail_recent - tail_base) - (ordinary_recent - ordinary_base)
        hidden_tail = _cross_sectional_residual(tail_innovation, semibeta)
        hidden_risk = rank(hidden_tail).sub(0.5).fillna(0.0)

        stock_vol = stock_ret.rolling(63, min_periods=30).std(ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        market = _market_panel(market_ret, close.columns)
        relative_move = (stock_ret - market) / stock_vol
        capitulation = (-relative_move).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)
        incomplete_decline = relative_move.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).fillna(0.0)

        rebound_leg = visible_risk * capitulation
        unwind_leg = hidden_risk * incomplete_decline
        activation = _fear_activation(market_ret)
        signal = (rebound_leg - unwind_leg).mul(activation, axis=0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close)

The interaction separates exhausted visible-risk selling from latent nonlinear-risk discovery, resolving Parent B's reversed empirical direction rather than simply flipping its sign. Parent A identifies the delayed-unwind leg but not the oversold high-semibeta rebound, while Parent B's semibeta sort alone cannot distinguish completed liquidation from hidden-tail shelters.

Tail-correlation innovation is cross-sectionally residualized against downside semibeta before interacting with relative shock direction.

"""Hidden tail-risk repricing among names previously viewed as beta-safe.

Mechanism: a stock may look safe under conventional downside-beta estimates while
its nonlinear co-crash frequency rises sharply in a market fear episode.  If it
also falls less than the market on the triggering day, delayed risk-budget and
risk-parity deleveraging should produce relative underperformance."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast(series: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    values = np.repeat(series.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(values, index=series.index, columns=columns)


def _market_zscore(series: pd.Series, window: int, minimum: int) -> pd.Series:
    mean = series.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    std = series.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).std(ddof=0)
    return (series - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _masked_beta(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    market_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    min_events: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing beta estimated only on observations selected by event."""
    valid = stock_ret.notna() & market_ret.notna() & event.fillna(False)
    weight = valid.astype(float)
    x = market_ret.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    y = stock_ret.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    count = weight.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sx = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sy = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    safe_count = count.where(count >= float(min_events))
    cov = sxy - sx * sy / safe_count
    var = sxx - sx * sx / safe_count
    return cov / var.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _conditional_tail_rate(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    stock_cutoff: pd.DataFrame,
    market_event: pd.Series,
    window: int,
    min_events: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing P(stock lower-tail event | market lower-tail event)."""
    event_panel = _broadcast(market_event.astype(float), stock_ret.columns).astype(bool)
    valid = event_panel & stock_ret.notna() & stock_cutoff.notna()
    hits = ((stock_ret <= stock_cutoff) & valid).astype(float)
    observations = valid.astype(float)
    numerator = hits.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    denominator = observations.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(denominator >= float(min_events))


def _tail_rate(
    stock_ret: pd.DataFrame,
    stock_cutoff: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing unconditional lower-tail frequency, used to remove volatility effects."""
    valid = stock_ret.notna() & stock_cutoff.notna()
    hits = ((stock_ret <= stock_cutoff) & valid).astype(float)
    count = valid.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return hits.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum() / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class HiddenTailBetaSafeDeleveragingGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "hidden_tail_beta_safe_deleveraging_gap"
    name = "Hidden Tail-Safe Deleveraging Gap"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "On market fear-tail days, identifies nominally downside-beta-safe stocks "
        "whose nonlinear co-crash probability has increased and whose current "
        "drawdown has not yet reflected that newly revealed systemic exposure."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = ret.clip(lower=-0.50, upper=0.50)
        market_ret = ret.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        market_panel = _broadcast(market_ret, close.columns)

        intraday_range = ((high - low).abs() / close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        market_range = intraday_range.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        rel_volume = volume.sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / volume_base.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        fear = (
            _market_zscore(-market_ret, 60, 30)
            + _market_zscore(market_range, 60, 30)
            + _market_zscore(rel_volume, 60, 30)
        ) / 3.0

        market_cutoff = market_ret.rolling(126, min_periods=80).quantile(0.20)
        market_tail = (market_ret <= market_cutoff) & market_ret.notna()
        stock_cutoff = ret.rolling(126, min_periods=80).quantile(0.20)

        conditional_recent = _conditional_tail_rate(ret, stock_cutoff, market_tail, 42, 5)
        conditional_base = _conditional_tail_rate(ret, stock_cutoff, market_tail, 126, 15)
        ordinary_recent = _tail_rate(ret, stock_cutoff, 42)
        ordinary_base = _tail_rate(ret, stock_cutoff, 126)
        tail_innovation = (conditional_recent - conditional_base) - (ordinary_recent - ordinary_base)
        tail_innovation = tail_innovation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        downside_beta = _masked_beta(
            ret, market_panel, _broadcast(market_tail.astype(float), close.columns).astype(bool), 126, 15
        )
        ordinary_beta = _masked_beta(
            ret,
            market_panel,
            pd.DataFrame(True, index=close.index, columns=close.columns),
            126,
            70,
        )
        beta_safety = (-(downside_beta - ordinary_beta)).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        stock_vol = ret.rolling(63, min_periods=30).std()
        incomplete_drawdown = ((ret - market_panel) / stock_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        incomplete_drawdown = incomplete_drawdown.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        shock_size = ((market_cutoff - market_ret) / market_ret.rolling(126, min_periods=63).std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        shock_size = shock_size.where(market_tail, 0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)
        fear_gate = ((fear - 0.25).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0) / 3.0).fillna(0.0)
        active = market_tail & fear_gate.gt(0.0)

        hidden_risk = tail_innovation * beta_safety * incomplete_drawdown
        hidden_risk = hidden_risk.mul(shock_size * fear_gate, axis=0)
        signal = (-hidden_risk).rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)
        signal = signal.mul(active, axis=0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Hidden Tail-Safe Deleveraging Gap
programs.trading_idea: The child targets names that appeared historically safe in downside-beta space relative to their ordinary beta, but whose recent downside co-crash probability has abruptly risen during a broad fear shock. These are hidden systemic-risk proxies: conventional beta models and prior risk budgets still treat them as defensive, while nonlinear tail linkage reveals that their protection is unreliable. A muted same-day decline creates a transmission gap, so subsequent de-risking should penalize these names more than either high-beta names already recognized by Parent A or generic tail-dependent names in Parent B.
programs.description: During an active market downside-tail shock, the factor measures each stock's recent innovation in conditional co-crash frequency net of its ordinary downside frequency. It shorts stocks with high hidden tail-linkage innovation, unusually low conditional beta versus ordinary beta, and an incomplete contemporaneous drawdown; it buys the opposite side.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each stock's contemporaneous sector mean using static labels."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)]
        if len(cols) == 0:
            continue
        group_mean = values.loc[:, cols].mean(axis=1)
        result.loc[:, cols] = np.asarray(group_mean)[:, None]
    return result


def _peer_underreaction_signal(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal peer-news relay with a finite reporting-firm exclusion window."""
    surprise = eps_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    estimate = eps_estimate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    fresh = surprise.notna() & (surprise.ne(previous) | previous.isna())

    scale = estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01).fillna(0.01)
    standardized = (surprise / scale).clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)
    event_news = standardized.where(fresh, np.nan)

    sector_event_news = _sector_mean(event_news, sector).fillna(0.0)
    sector_news = sector_event_news.ewm(halflife=2.5, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

    two_day_return = close.pct_change(2).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    sector_return = _sector_mean(two_day_return, sector)
    relative_reaction = (two_day_return - sector_return).clip(lower=-0.35, upper=0.35)

    news_sign = np.sign(sector_news)
    opposite_reaction = (-news_sign * relative_reaction).clip(lower=0.0)
    relay = news_sign * sector_news.abs() * opposite_reaction

    reporting_lockout = fresh.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).max()
    relay = relay.where(reporting_lockout.eq(0.0), 0.0)
    relay = relay.where(sector_news.abs() > 0.002, 0.0)
    return relay.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class PeerEarningsUnderreactionRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_earnings_underreaction_relay"
    name = "Peer Earnings Underreaction Relay"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Sector earnings-news diffusion into non-reporting peers that have "
        "underreacted in sector-relative returns."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "epsSurprise", "epsEstimate", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        signal = _peer_underreaction_signal(
            close,
            data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close),
            data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close),
            data["sector"].reindex_like(close),
        )
        return rank(signal).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: Earnings announcements reveal information not only about the reporting firm but also about demand, costs, and competitive conditions for its sector peers. A sector-level surprise should diffuse most strongly into peers whose recent sector-relative price reaction is in the wrong direction or absent, because analysts and benchmarked investors must map issuer-specific news into peer-level earnings implications over several sessions. The edge should persist because this inference is noisy and heterogeneous across firms, making immediate arbitrage difficult; it is falsified if peers that initially underreact to signed sector earnings news do not subsequently move in the direction of that news over the next six sessions.

Reporting firms are temporarily excluded so the signal expresses peer-information diffusion rather than direct post-earnings drift.

"""Delayed residual-capitulation repair after observable selling exhaustion.

Mechanism: broad fear can generate idiosyncratic forced sales in otherwise resilient
firms, but the initial shock can continue for a bar or two as risk limits and
redemption orders are completed.  The factor waits for a prior residual downside and
participation burst, then requires recent residual selling intensity to decelerate.
This identifies liquidation completion rather than attempting to catch the initial
falling knife.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _zscore(value: pd.DataFrame, window: int, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal, bounded trailing z-score."""
    mean = value.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean()
    std = value.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).std()
    return ((value - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)


def _lagged_market_residual(
    stock_returns: pd.DataFrame, market_state: pd.Series, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residual to a market-fear state using coefficients known before today."""
    minimum = max(30, window // 2)
    mean_y = stock_returns.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean().shift(1)
    mean_x = market_state.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).mean().shift(1)
    mean_xy = stock_returns.mul(market_state, axis=0).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean().shift(1)
    mean_x2 = (market_state * market_state).rolling(
        window, min_periods=minimum
    ).mean().shift(1)

    covariance = mean_xy.sub(mean_y.mul(mean_x, axis=0), axis=0)
    variance = mean_x2 - mean_x * mean_x
    beta = covariance.div(variance.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    fitted = mean_y + beta.mul(market_state - mean_x, axis=0)
    return stock_returns - fitted


def _resilience_score(
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
    fcf_yield: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional financing resilience with neutral treatment of sparse data."""
    cash = cash_ratio.where(cash_ratio >= 0.0)
    current = current_ratio.where(current_ratio >= 0.0)
    debt = debt_to_equity.where(debt_to_equity >= 0.0)
    fcf = fcf_yield.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    return (
        rank(cash).fillna(0.5)
        + rank(current).fillna(0.5)
        + (1.0 - rank(debt).fillna(0.5))
        + rank(fcf).fillna(0.5)
    ).div(4.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class FearResidualExhaustionConfirmationH6(BaseFactor):
    """Delayed repair of completed fear-related idiosyncratic liquidation."""

    factor_id = "fear_residual_exhaustion_confirmation_h6"
    name = "Fear-Residual Exhaustion Confirmation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Ranks resilient firms after a recent fear-related residual selloff and "
        "volume burst only once their residual downside pressure has decelerated."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "cashRatio",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close).astype(float).clip(lower=0.0)
        stock_returns = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        market_return = stock_returns.median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        market_volume = np.log1p(volume.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1))
        market_return_z = _zscore(market_return.to_frame("market"), 42, 21).iloc[:, 0]
        market_volume_z = _zscore(market_volume.to_frame("volume"), 42, 21).iloc[:, 0]
        fear = (
            (-market_return_z.fillna(0.0)).clip(lower=0.0)
            + 0.35 * market_volume_z.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        ).clip(upper=5.0)

        residual = _lagged_market_residual(stock_returns, fear, 84)
        residual_z = _zscore(residual, 20, 10)
        negative_pressure = (-residual_z).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        prior_pressure = negative_pressure.shift(2).rolling(
            4, min_periods=3
        ).mean()
        recent_pressure = negative_pressure.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
        exhaustion = (prior_pressure - recent_pressure).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        volume_z = _zscore(np.log1p(volume.fillna(0.0)), 20, 10)
        prior_participation = volume_z.shift(2).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0).rolling(
            4, min_periods=3
        ).max()

        recent_fear = fear.shift(2).rolling(4, min_periods=3).mean()
        resilience = _resilience_score(
            data["cashRatio"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
            data["currentRatio"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
            data["debtToEquity"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
            data["freeCashFlowYield"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
        )

        qualified = (
            (prior_pressure > 0.75)
            & (prior_participation > 0.50)
            & (exhaustion > 0.35)
        )
        raw = (
            rank(prior_pressure).fillna(0.5)
            * rank(prior_participation).fillna(0.5)
            * rank(exhaustion).fillna(0.5)
            * resilience
        ).where(qualified)

        fear_active = (recent_fear >= 0.75).astype(float)
        signal = (rank(raw).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).mul(fear_active, axis=0)
        return signal.reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The parent appears to identify genuine forced selling, but its negative 1-bar IC indicates that buying the initial capitulation is too early. This child waits until a broad-fear-driven, stock-specific residual selloff and its abnormal participation occurred several days earlier, then enters only when residual downside pressure has materially decelerated; this targets the delayed completion of liquidation rather than the falling-knife phase. The edge should persist because risk-limit selling and fund redemptions are mechanically spread across several sessions, while arbitrageurs require observable exhaustion before committing capital to names with substantial residual-risk uncertainty.
programs.description: Ranks financially resilient stocks whose idiosyncratic downside residual and volume shock occurred two to five bars ago during broad fear, but whose recent residual selling pressure has decelerated. The signal is active only in a recent market-fear regime and is designed to capture delayed post-capitulation repair at six bars.

"""Downside innovation clusters identify persistent endogenous sell pressure.

Mechanism: recurrent negative return innovations are consistent with asymmetric
self-excitation in sell orders.  Unlike an isolated information shock, a
cluster can reflect constrained liquidation and delayed dealer inventory
adjustment, which may continue to pressure prices over the next week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _downside_cluster_intensity(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal marked-event intensity for recurring downside return shocks.

    The volatility scale is lagged, preventing the current shock from reducing
    its own standardized magnitude.  A short EW intensity is compared with a
    slower, pre-current baseline and is retained only when preceding downside
    events establish a cluster rather than a single news jump.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    log_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))

    lagged_scale = log_return.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=15).std()
    standardized_downside = (-log_return / lagged_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    mark = standardized_downside.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

    # Event density is strictly pre-current: an isolated event cannot qualify
    # as a self-exciting cluster merely because it is large today.
    prior_event_density = (
        (mark > 1.0).astype(float).shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean().fillna(0.0)
    )
    fast_intensity = mark.ewm(halflife=2.5, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
    slow_baseline = mark.shift(1).ewm(halflife=12.0, adjust=False, min_periods=8).mean()

    excess_intensity = (fast_intensity - slow_baseline).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
    return (excess_intensity * prior_event_density).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class DownsideInnovationClusterContinuation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "downside_innovation_cluster_continuation"
    name = "Downside Innovation Cluster Continuation"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks recurrent volatility-scaled downside return innovations: a fast "
        "downside intensity above its prior baseline, gated by prior downside "
        "event density. Higher scores predict lower six-bar returns."
    )
    window_length = 30
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        raw_signal = _downside_cluster_intensity(close)
        output = rank(raw_signal)
        return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Downside Innovation Cluster Continuation
programs.trading_idea: Clusters of downside volatility innovations proxy for self-exciting sell pressure: margin calls, risk-limit reductions, and liquidity-provider withdrawal cause one negative shock to raise the probability of further negative shocks. The signal explicitly suppresses isolated bad-news moves and activates only when abnormal negative returns recur, so it targets endogenous order-flow persistence rather than generic volatility. The edge should persist because constrained sellers and dealer inventory adjustment cannot be instantaneously arbitraged away; it is falsified if high cluster scores do not predict relatively lower six-bar returns after conditioning on recent return and volatility.
programs.description: Measures the excess of a fast exponentially weighted intensity of volatility-scaled negative returns over its slower pre-event baseline, multiplied by the density of prior downside shocks. High values identify recurrent, self-exciting downside innovation clusters.
