"""Auction rejection repair with an earnings-information veto.

Mechanism: a downward opening gap that is rejected by the close can be an
inventory overshoot during synchronized sector selling.  A fresh, large negative
earnings-anchored move confirmed by industry peers is instead treated as
information, so it vetoes the reversal trade.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _clean(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _ewma(events: pd.DataFrame, half_life: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    alpha = 1.0 - np.exp(np.log(0.5) / half_life)
    return events.fillna(0.0).astype(float).ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean()

def _leave_one_out_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional leave-one-out group average at each date."""
    lab = labels.iloc[0].reindex(values.columns).astype(object)
    lab = lab.where(lab.notna(), '__MISSING_GROUP__')
    key = lab.to_numpy()
    valid = values.notna().astype(float)
    group_sum = values.fillna(0.0).T.groupby(key, sort=False).sum().T
    group_count = valid.T.groupby(key, sort=False).sum().T
    mapped_sum = group_sum.reindex(columns=key)
    mapped_count = group_count.reindex(columns=key)
    mapped_sum.columns = values.columns
    mapped_count.columns = values.columns
    return (mapped_sum - values.fillna(0.0)) / (mapped_count - valid).where(mapped_count - valid > 0.0)

def _report_event(fields: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=fields[0].index, columns=fields[0].columns)
    for field in fields:
        previous = field.shift(1)
        changed = field.notna() & (previous.isna() | field.ne(previous))
        event = event | changed.fillna(False)
    return event

@register_factor
class AuctionRejectionEarningsVetoFlowRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'auction_rejection_earnings_veto_flow_repair_1'
    name = 'Auction Rejection Earnings-Veto Repair'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Longs rejected downside auction gaps during synchronized sell pressure, but discounts fresh negative earnings displacements confirmed by industry peers.'
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'sector', 'industry', 'epsActual', 'revenueActual', 'epsSurprise', 'revenueSurprise']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float)
        high = data['high'].astype(float)
        low = data['low'].astype(float)
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        daily_return = _clean(close / prior_close - 1.0)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().shift(1)
        relative_volume = _clean(volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ret_center = daily_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().shift(1)
        ret_scale = daily_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().shift(1)
        ret_z = _clean((daily_return - ret_center) / ret_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        negative_arrival = ((relative_volume >= 1.4) & (ret_z <= -0.75)).astype(float)
        positive_arrival = ((relative_volume >= 1.4) & (ret_z >= 0.75)).astype(float)
        sell_clock = _ewma(negative_arrival, 4.0) - _ewma(positive_arrival, 4.0)
        sell_clock = sell_clock.clip(lower=0.0)
        relative_range = _clean((high - low).abs() / safe_close)
        range_mean = relative_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        range_std = relative_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().shift(1)
        range_z = _clean((relative_range - range_mean) / range_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        volume_mean = volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        volume_std = volume.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().shift(1)
        volume_z = _clean((volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        stress_event = ((range_z > 1.0) & (volume_z > 1.0)).astype(float)
        peer_stress = _leave_one_out_mean(stress_event, data['sector'])
        stress_mean = peer_stress.rolling(60, min_periods=30).mean().shift(1)
        stress_std = peer_stress.rolling(60, min_periods=30).std().shift(1)
        synchrony = _clean((peer_stress - stress_mean) / stress_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        sector_return = _leave_one_out_mean(daily_return, data['sector'])
        residual_return = daily_return - sector_return
        residual_scale = residual_return.rolling(20, min_periods=10).std().shift(1)
        idio_downside = _clean(-residual_return / residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        gap = _clean((open_ - prior_close) / prior_close)
        body = _clean((close - open_) / safe_open)
        session_range = _clean((high - low).abs() / prior_close)
        gap_scale = session_range.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        down_gap = _clean(-gap / gap_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 5.0)
        rejection = _clean(body / session_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        event = _report_event([data['epsActual'].astype(float), data['revenueActual'].astype(float), data['epsSurprise'].astype(float), data['revenueSurprise'].astype(float)])
        fresh_event = event.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max()
        event_anchor = close.shift(1).where(event & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)).ffill()
        displacement = _clean(np.log(close / event_anchor.replace(0.0, np.nan)))
        normal_move = daily_return.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=25).quantile(0.8)
        tail_displacement = _clean(displacement.abs() / normal_move.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        industry_return = _leave_one_out_mean(daily_return.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum(), data['industry'])
        peer_confirms = (displacement * industry_return > 0.0).astype(float)
        earnings_veto = (fresh_event * (displacement < 0.0).astype(float) * (tail_displacement >= 1.0).astype(float) * peer_confirms).fillna(0.0)
        absorption = down_gap * rejection
        raw = absorption * sell_clock * synchrony * idio_downside / (1.0 + earnings_veto)
        eligible = (gap < 0.0) & (body > 0.0) & (sell_clock > 0.0) & (synchrony > 0.0)
        signal = rank(_clean(raw.where(eligible))).sub(0.5)
        return signal.fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: The child buys a downside opening-auction dislocation only when the gap is rejected by the close and occurs inside a sector-synchronous, persistent sell-flow episode, identifying a likely temporary inventory shock. It then applies an earnings-information veto: a fresh, large negative earnings-anchored displacement that is directionally confirmed by industry peers is treated as information rather than forced selling. The interaction carries edge because Parent A's auction absorption is unsafe around validated earnings news, while Parent B's news filter becomes actionable only when it selectively protects a mechanically absorbed auction reversal.
programs.description: Ranks rejected downside opening gaps with persistent negative volume arrivals, sector stress synchrony, and idiosyncratic downside, while down-weighting fresh earnings-linked negative moves confirmed by industry returns. The factor is long likely forced-sale auction overshoots and avoids confirmed informational repricing.

"""Asymmetric volatility innovation as a deleveraging-flow signal.

Mechanism: a large negative bar near its low becomes a continuation signal when
negative realized variance accelerates relative to its own slow baseline and
participation is elevated.  This state proxies risk-limit and margin-driven
selling, whose execution commonly extends over several daily bars.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _asymmetric_volatility_innovation(ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal ratio of fast to slow downside variance, net of upside variance."""
    negative_sq = ret.where(ret < 0.0, 0.0).pow(2)
    positive_sq = ret.where(ret > 0.0, 0.0).pow(2)
    fast_down = negative_sq.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=8).mean()
    slow_down = negative_sq.ewm(halflife=24.0, adjust=False, min_periods=20).mean()
    fast_up = positive_sq.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=8).mean()
    slow_up = positive_sq.ewm(halflife=24.0, adjust=False, min_periods=20).mean()
    down_innovation = np.log((fast_down + 1e-10) / (slow_down + 1e-10))
    up_innovation = np.log((fast_up + 1e-10) / (slow_up + 1e-10))
    return (down_innovation - up_innovation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

@register_factor
class AsymmetricVolatilityInnovationDeleveragingDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'asymmetric_volatility_innovation_deleveraging_dr'
    name = 'Asymmetric Volatility Deleveraging Drift'
    category = 'volatility'
    description = 'High downside-volatility innovation, abnormal participation, and a close near the daily low identify ongoing deleveraging pressure; higher values predict weaker subsequent returns.'
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        high = data['high'].astype(float)
        low = data['low'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float)
        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return_scale = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std().shift(1)
        downside_size = (-ret / return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        vol_innovation = _asymmetric_volatility_innovation(ret).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))
        volume_mean = log_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
        volume_std = log_volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        volume_z = (log_volume - volume_mean) / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = volume_z.clip(0.0, 3.0)
        daily_range = (high - low).where(high - low > 0.0)
        close_location = ((close - low) / daily_range).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        low_close_pressure = (1.0 - close_location).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        eligible = (ret < 0.0) & (vol_innovation > 0.0) & (participation > 0.0) & (low_close_pressure > 0.0)
        raw = downside_size * vol_innovation * participation * low_close_pressure
        signal = rank(raw.where(eligible)).sub(0.5)
        return signal.fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Asymmetric Volatility Deleveraging Drift
programs.trading_idea: A negative return that closes near the session low is more likely to continue when it coincides with an unusually rapid increase in downside, rather than symmetric, volatility and elevated participation. This identifies a leverage-constrained deleveraging state: rising downside variance raises risk limits and margin demand, causing institutions to sell over several subsequent sessions rather than fully clear inventory immediately. The hypothesis is falsifiable because the short-side effect should be concentrated in high downside-volatility-innovation, high-volume, low-close-location observations and should disappear or reverse when volatility is symmetric or the bar closes away from its low; it persists against arbitrage because the marginal seller is risk-constrained rather than an unconstrained information trader.
programs.description: Ranks stocks by a causal asymmetric volatility-innovation measure, activated only for negative returns that close near the low on abnormal volume. Higher signal values denote acute downside deleveraging pressure and are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.

"""Temporary rebound after isolated downside liquidity demand.

Mechanism: an idiosyncratic downside shock with unusually high participation can
reflect a persistent stock-specific sell program.  A close near the day's high
shows immediate liquidity absorption, but when the shock is not shared by the
sector that rebound can be a dealer-inventory relay rather than completed
information assimilation, leaving further downside over the following week.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _leave_one_out_sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-bar leave-one-out sector mean for static classifications."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    safe_labels = labels.reindex(values.columns).fillna('__unknown_sector__')
    for group in pd.unique(safe_labels):
        cols = safe_labels.index[safe_labels == group]
        block = values.loc[:, cols]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        total = block.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        peer = block.rsub(total, axis=0).div(count.sub(1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        out.loc[:, cols] = peer
    return out

def _downside_innovation(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fast-versus-slow causal downside semivariance innovation."""
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    downside_sq = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.25).pow(2).fillna(0.0)
    fast = downside_sq.ewm(halflife=2.0, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
    slow = downside_sq.ewm(halflife=20.0, adjust=False, min_periods=15).mean()
    return (fast / slow.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

@register_factor
class IsolatedDownsideAbsorptionRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'isolated_downside_absorption_relay_j'
    name = 'Isolated Downside Absorption Relay'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'High values identify high-volume, idiosyncratic downside-volatility shocks that recover within the bar, a temporary absorption state expected to relay into subsequent selling.'
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'sector', 'roic', 'freeCashFlowYield']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        high = data['high'].where(data['high'].notna(), close)
        low = data['low'].where(data['low'].notna(), close)
        volume = data['volume'].clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        safe_close = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0)
        norm_range = (bar_range / safe_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        range_base = norm_range.rolling(36, min_periods=20).mean()
        range_innovation = norm_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        sector_labels = data['sector'].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        peer_innovation = _leave_one_out_sector_mean(range_innovation, sector_labels)
        isolated_range = (range_innovation - peer_innovation).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        isolation_gate = np.tanh(isolated_range)
        innovation = _downside_innovation(close)
        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        own_vol = ret.rolling(29, min_periods=15).std()
        downside_move = (-ret / own_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        downside_gate = np.tanh(downside_move / 2.0)
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        recovery_gate = ((close_location - 0.5) * 2.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        volume_base = volume.rolling(29, min_periods=10).mean()
        volume_surprise = (volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        participation_gate = np.tanh(volume_surprise / 2.0)
        roic_rank = rank(data['roic'].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)).fillna(0.0)
        fcf_rank = rank(data['freeCashFlowYield'].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)).fillna(0.0)
        quality = (roic_rank + fcf_rank) / 2.0
        signal = (innovation * downside_gate * isolation_gate * recovery_gate * participation_gate * quality).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic downside-range shock that closes near the bar high is not necessarily completed selling: it can be a temporary liquidity-provider rebound while a stock-specific institutional sell program remains active. The negative realized signs of both parents are consistent with this interpretation: isolated flow and intrabar resilience identify a deceptive absorption phase rather than durable recovery, with dealers and slower participants subsequently re-hedging inventory over the next week. The interaction carries edge because sector isolation distinguishes name-specific supply from broad risk-off volatility, while close-location recovery identifies the transient bounce within that otherwise persistent sell-pressure episode; neither condition alone identifies this relay state.

Higher values identify temporary absorption of idiosyncratic sell pressure and are expected to precede lower six-bar returns.

"""Conditional leverage-response residual as a downside-amplification signal.

Mechanism: a large range is expected after a prior negative return because of the
leverage effect.  A range materially above that trailing conditional expectation,
when accompanied by a fresh sell shock and clustered prior downside flow, instead
indicates endogenous liquidity withdrawal and constrained inventory reduction.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _amplification_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal conditional-range residual times a clustered downside shock."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0, np.nan)
    safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0, np.nan)
    safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    # Log range is a stable daily realized-volatility proxy.  The covariate is
    # known at the preceding close, so the conditional response is causal.
    log_range = np.log(safe_high / safe_low).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50)
    lagged_downside = (-ret.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.15)
    x_mean = lagged_downside.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
    y_mean = log_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).mean()
    x_var = lagged_downside.rolling(40, min_periods=20).var()
    xy_cov = lagged_downside.rolling(40, min_periods=20).cov(log_range)
    leverage_beta = (xy_cov / x_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=10.0)
    expected_range = y_mean + leverage_beta * (lagged_downside - x_mean)
    residual_scale = log_range.rolling(40, min_periods=20).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    range_residual = ((log_range - expected_range) / residual_scale).clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)

    downside = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.15)
    semivol = np.sqrt((downside * downside).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean())
    sell_shock = (downside / semivol.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

    # This is an exponentially decayed, marked-event intensity estimated only
    # from completed prior bars; it distinguishes isolated bad days from a flow cluster.
    prior_flow = downside.shift(1).ewm(halflife=4, adjust=False, min_periods=5).mean()
    flow_intensity = (prior_flow / semivol.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

    clean_volume = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
    volume_base = clean_volume.ewm(halflife=20, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
    relative_volume = (clean_volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)
    participation = np.sqrt(relative_volume)

    return sell_shock * range_residual.clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 + flow_intensity) * participation


@register_factor
class LeverageResponseRangeResidualShort(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "leverage_response_range_residual_short"
    name = "Leverage Response Range Residual"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "High values identify fresh downside shocks whose intraday range exceeds "
        "their trailing leverage-effect expectation amid clustered selling and high participation."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        state = _amplification_state(
            close,
            data["high"].astype(float),
            data["low"].astype(float),
            data["volume"].astype(float),
        )
        ranked = state.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5).astype(float)
programs.name: Leverage Response Range Residual
programs.trading_idea: Negative returns normally raise subsequent volatility through the leverage effect, but an unusually large realized range after controlling for that expected response indicates an endogenous liquidity withdrawal rather than an ordinary repricing. When this residual range expansion coincides with a fresh downside shock, elevated participation, and preceding negative-flow clustering, dealers and risk-managed investors continue to reduce exposure over the next week, producing negative return continuation. The hypothesis is falsifiable: conditional on equally large negative returns, names with positive leverage-response range residuals should underperform names whose ranges are fully explained by their own trailing leverage response; the edge persists because short-sale constraints, margin policies, and dealer inventory adjustment prevent instantaneous correction.
programs.description: Ranks stocks by a downside-volatility feedback state: a current standardized sell shock multiplied by the unexpected component of its intraday range after a trailing conditional leverage model, prior downside-flow intensity, and relative volume. from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _excess_systemic_tail_coincidence(ret: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal nonlinear co-crash dependence relative to routine down days.

    A stock's lower-tail event is defined from its own trailing return history.
    The signal is its smoothed conditional tail-event probability on aggregate
    market-tail days less the analogous probability on non-tail negative market
    days. This removes much of ordinary downside beta and retains crash-specific
    dependence relevant under heavy-tailed marginal utility.
    """
    market = ret.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    market_cut = market.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).quantile(0.15)
    stock_cut = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).quantile(0.20)

    market_tail = market.le(market_cut) & market.notna() & market_cut.notna()
    routine_down = market.lt(0.0) & market.gt(market_cut) & market_cut.notna()

    tail_mask = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(market_tail.to_numpy()[:, None], ret.shape),
        index=ret.index,
        columns=ret.columns,
    )
    routine_mask = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(routine_down.to_numpy()[:, None], ret.shape),
        index=ret.index,
        columns=ret.columns,
    )

    eligible = ret.notna() & stock_cut.notna()
    own_tail = ret.le(stock_cut) & eligible

    tail_trials = (eligible & tail_mask).astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum()
    routine_trials = (eligible & routine_mask).astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum()
    tail_hits = (own_tail & tail_mask).astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum()
    routine_hits = (own_tail & routine_mask).astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).sum()

    # Jeffreys smoothing prevents sparse conditional frequencies from dominating.
    tail_probability = (tail_hits + 0.5) / (tail_trials + 1.0)
    routine_probability = (routine_hits + 0.5) / (routine_trials + 1.0)
    excess = tail_probability - routine_probability

    return excess.where((tail_trials >= 12.0) & (routine_trials >= 24.0)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class SystemicTailCoincidenceCashflowPremium(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "systemic_tail_coincidence_cashflow_premium"
    name = "Systemic Tail Coincidence Premium"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Ranks nonlinear excess co-crash probability relative to ordinary down "
        "days, scaled toward firms with stronger free-cash-flow yield and "
        "operating-cash-flow quality."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "freeCashFlowYield", "incomeQuality"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        tail_excess = _excess_systemic_tail_coincidence(ret, 126)

        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].reindex_like(close)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].reindex_like(close)
        fcf_yield = fcf_yield.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        income_quality = income_quality.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        tail_rank = tail_excess.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        value_rank = fcf_yield.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        quality_rank = income_quality.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        cashflow_strength = 0.5 * value_rank + 0.5 * quality_rank

        score = tail_rank * cashflow_strength
        return score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5).astype(float)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank


def _tail_gate(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    ret = close.replace(0.0, np.nan).pct_change(fill_method=None)
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market = ret.median(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
    values = market.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    inverse_alpha = np.full(len(values), np.nan, dtype=float)
    window = 63
    extremes = 10
    for t in range(window - 1, len(values)):
        sample = values[t - window + 1:t + 1]
        losses = -sample[np.isfinite(sample) & (sample < 0.0)]
        if losses.size < extremes:
            continue
        ordered = np.sort(losses)[::-1]
        threshold = ordered[extremes - 1]
        if threshold <= 1.0e-12:
            continue
        logs = np.log(ordered[:extremes] / threshold)
        total = float(np.nansum(logs))
        if total > 1.0e-12:
            inverse_alpha[t] = total / float(extremes)

    hill = pd.Series(inverse_alpha, index=close.index)
    hill_mean = hill.rolling(126, min_periods=63).mean()
    hill_std = hill.rolling(126, min_periods=63).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    hill_z = ((hill - hill_mean) / hill_std).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    downside = (-market).clip(lower=0.0)
    stress = downside.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
    stress_mean = stress.rolling(63, min_periods=30).mean()
    stress_std = stress.rolling(63, min_periods=30).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    stress_z = ((stress - stress_mean) / stress_std).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    state = (1.1 * hill_z.fillna(-3.0) + 0.9 * stress_z.fillna(-3.0)).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-state))


def _fresh_ranked_update(field: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    clean = field.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    change = clean.diff(1)
    event = change.abs() > 1.0e-12
    innovation = (change.where(event).rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 0.5).fillna(0.0)
    decayed = innovation.ewm(halflife=2.0, adjust=False).mean()
    recent = event.astype(float).rolling(4, min_periods=1).max()
    return decayed, recent


def _group_residual(value: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    valid = value.notna()
    row_median = value.median(axis=1)
    filled = value.T.fillna(row_median).T.fillna(0.0)
    return indneutralize(filled, groups).where(valid)


def _quietness(close: pd.DataFrame, high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ret = close.replace(0.0, np.nan).pct_change(fill_method=None)
    downside_vol = ret.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2.0).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().pow(0.5)
    log_range = np.log(high.where(high > 0.0) / low.where(low > 0.0))
    range_vol = (log_range.pow(2.0).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean() / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))).pow(0.5)
    quiet_downside = rank(-_group_residual(downside_vol, sector)).fillna(0.5)
    quiet_range = rank(-_group_residual(range_vol, sector)).fillna(0.5)
    return 0.5 * (quiet_downside + quiet_range)


@register_factor
class TailRegimeQualityDissonanceResolution(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'tail_regime_quality_dissonance_resolution'
    name = 'Tail-Regime Quality Dissonance Resolution'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Tail-risk-gated quality-disclosure dissonance: trade fresh quality updates '
        'opposing industry-relative price action, with the sign-specific weight set '
        'by quiet-path fragility or resilience.'
    )
    window_length = 189
    inputs = [
        'close', 'high', 'low', 'sector', 'industry', 'roic', 'incomeQuality',
        'grossMargin', 'interestCoverage', 'netDebtToEbitda', 'debtToCapital',
        'currentRatio', 'operatingCashFlowGrowth'
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector = data['sector']
        industry = data['industry']

        updates = []
        recencies = []
        for field in [data['roic'], data['incomeQuality'], data['grossMargin']]:
            update, recent = _fresh_ranked_update(field)
            updates.append(update)
            recencies.append(recent)
        quality = sum(updates) / float(len(updates))
        freshness = sum(recencies) / float(len(recencies))

        coverage = data['interestCoverage'].clip(lower=-20.0, upper=30.0)
        net_debt = data['netDebtToEbitda'].clip(lower=-5.0, upper=25.0)
        debt_capital = data['debtToCapital'].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=2.0)
        current_ratio = data['currentRatio'].clip(lower=-1.0, upper=15.0)
        cashflow_growth = data['operatingCashFlowGrowth'].clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        fragility = (
            rank(-coverage).fillna(0.5) + rank(net_debt).fillna(0.5) +
            rank(debt_capital).fillna(0.5) + rank(-current_ratio).fillna(0.5) +
            rank(-cashflow_growth).fillna(0.5)
        ) / 5.0
        fragility = fragility.ewm(halflife=42.0, adjust=False).mean()

        quiet = _quietness(close, data['high'], data['low'], sector)
        prior_return = close.pct_change(5, fill_method=None)
        relative_return = _group_residual(prior_return, industry)
        price_rank = rank(relative_return).fillna(0.5) - 0.5
        disagreement = (-np.sign(quality) * price_rank).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.5)

        sign_state = (1.0 - fragility).where(quality >= 0.0, fragility)
        tail_weight = _tail_gate(close)
        raw = quality * disagreement * freshness * quiet * sign_state.mul(tail_weight, axis=0)
        eligible = freshness > 0.0
        neutral = indneutralize(raw.fillna(0.0), industry).where(eligible)
        return (rank(neutral).fillna(0.5) - 0.5).where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Aggregate heavy-left-tail states make investors especially sensitive to hidden cash-flow fragility, but Parent A's broad resilience signal can be crowded and ambiguously priced. This child trades fresh quality disclosures only when they contradict recent industry-relative price action and when the firm-specific quiet-path/financial-fragility state identifies whether the disclosure resolves latent tail exposure: bad news in fragile, compressed-risk firms should continue down, while good news in resilient firms that have underperformed should catch up. The interaction carries edge because the tail regime supplies the discount-rate urgency, while the contradiction and balance-sheet state identify the particular names for which the market has not yet incorporated the disclosure.

"""Nonlinear downside-coskewness compensation under heavy-tailed aggregate risk.

Mechanism: when aggregate consumption growth has heavy left tails, investors dislike
assets whose idiosyncratic losses are amplified specifically in severe market
drawdowns.  Stocks with high residual downside-tail loading should earn a premium
because this crash-state exposure is costly to insure and difficult to arbitrage.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _downside_coskew_loading(ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate residual loading on squared lower-tail market losses causally.

    A trailing linear beta first removes conventional market exposure.  The
    remaining loading is the negative residual return associated with squared
    market losses on dates belonging to the trailing lower quintile.
    """
    window = 120
    minimum = 60

    market = ret.mean(axis=1).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_var = market.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).var()
    market_cov = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).cov(market)
    beta = market_cov.div(market_var.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)

    residual = ret - beta.mul(market, axis=0)
    tail_cutoff = market.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).quantile(0.20)
    downside_loss = (-market.where(market <= tail_cutoff, 0.0)).clip(lower=0.0)
    tail_weight = downside_loss.pow(2)

    weighted_residual = residual.mul(tail_weight, axis=0)
    numerator = weighted_residual.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()
    denominator = tail_weight.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum).sum()

    return -numerator.div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)


@register_factor
class NonlinearDownsideCoskewCompensationH6(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "nonlinear_downside_coskew_compensation_h6"
    name = "Nonlinear Downside Coskew Compensation"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of residual downside-tail loading: long stocks "
        "whose returns are unusually negative during squared lower-tail market "
        "losses after removing ordinary trailing market beta."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].where(data["close"] > 0.0)
        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        loading = _downside_coskew_loading(ret)
        signal = rank(loading).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

This child estimates that nonlinear downside exposure from trailing daily returns and ranks stocks by their residual loss loading during market-tail observations. The premium can persist because crash-state risk is difficult for arbitrageurs to warehouse and is especially unattractive to investors with leveraged or consumption-sensitive liabilities; the hypothesis is falsified if high residual downside-tail loading does not precede higher six-bar returns after controlling for ordinary beta.

"""Fresh collection fragility conditioned on unabsorbed tail execution.

Mechanism: a newly disclosed rise in receivables relative to revenue makes an
otherwise ordinary downside event more informative because the firm's growth
narrative is less cash-backed.  A negative range shock that closes near the low
on unusually high volume is treated as unabsorbed execution pressure rather
than an isolated volatility event, so the joint episode predicts further
relative downside.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _quarterly_change(frame: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal change of a point-in-time quarterly step-function field."""
    prior = frame.shift(lag)
    return frame.sub(prior).div(prior.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))


def _freshness(frame: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally decayed state for a newly available fundamental observation."""
    prior = frame.shift(1)
    update = (frame.notna() & prior.notna() & frame.ne(prior)).astype(float)
    values = update.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros_like(values)
    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        if t == 0:
            state[t] = values[t]
        else:
            state[t] = np.maximum(values[t], decay * state[t - 1])
    return pd.DataFrame(state, index=frame.index, columns=frame.columns)


def _unabsorbed_tail_execution(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing-only mark for a downside tail event with execution confirmation."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close.div(previous_close).sub(1.0)
    realized_range = high.sub(low).abs().div(previous_close)

    volatility = ret.rolling(30, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
    downside_size = (-ret.clip(upper=0.0)).div(volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    downside_size = downside_size.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

    range_base = realized_range.rolling(30, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
    range_excess = realized_range.div(range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
    range_excess = range_excess.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

    bar_width = high.sub(low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    close_location = close.sub(low).div(bar_width).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    low_close_pressure = (1.0 - close_location).fillna(0.0)

    volume_base = volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
    volume_excess = volume.div(volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
    volume_excess = volume_excess.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

    return (downside_size * range_excess * low_close_pressure * volume_excess).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=200.0
    )


@register_factor
class FreshCollectionTailExecutionUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "fresh_collection_tail_execution_unwind"
    name = "Fresh Collection Tail-Execution Unwind"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-relative rank of fresh receivables-intensity deterioration "
        "interacted with an abnormal, volume-confirmed downside range event "
        "that closes near the low. High values forecast relative downside."
    )
    window_length = 93
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "receivables", "revenue", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        close = template.replace([np.inf, -np.inf, 0.0], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(template).where(
            data["high"].reindex_like(template).notna(), close
        )
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(template).where(
            data["low"].reindex_like(template).notna(), close
        )
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(template).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(template)

        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex_like(template)
        receivables = data["receivables"].reindex_like(template)
        collection_intensity = receivables.div(revenue.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        collection_change = _quarterly_change(collection_intensity, 63)
        collection_bad = collection_change.clip(lower=0.0)
        fresh = _freshness(collection_intensity, 0.85)

        execution_mark = _unabsorbed_tail_execution(close, high, low, volume)
        collection_rank = rank(collection_bad).fillna(0.5)
        execution_rank = rank(execution_mark).fillna(0.5)

        active = (
            collection_bad.gt(0.0)
            & execution_mark.gt(0.0)
            & fresh.gt(0.0)
        )
        raw = (collection_rank * execution_rank * fresh).where(active, 0.0)
        industry_relative = indneutralize(raw, industry)
        return rank(industry_relative).reindex_like(template).fillna(0.5)

A left-tail return/range event that closes near the low on abnormal volume is instead evidence of unabsorbed execution demand and liquidity depletion; conditioning that event on the fresh collection break isolates repricings where marginal buyers are least willing to provide support. The interaction has edge because collection weakness alone lacks a catalyst and a generic downside shock can rebound, whereas a cash-quality break accompanied by persistent sell-side execution is more likely to continue over the next week.

"""Tail-cluster refinancing deleveraging.

Mechanism: clustered aggregate left-tail shocks reveal the heavy-tailed consumption
risk state in which financially fragile firms face constrained refinancing and
forced portfolio sales.  Recent systematic co-crashes identify names currently
in that deleveraging channel, so high scores predict lower near-term returns.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _tail_cluster_pressure(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal stock-specific pressure from clustered market left-tail days.

    A market tail day is defined using only the trailing 126-bar empirical
    15th percentile.  Pressure requires both a recent co-crash and a stock's
    trailing propensity to participate in market-tail events.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market = ret.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    tail_cutoff = market.rolling(126, min_periods=80).quantile(0.15)
    market_tail = market.le(tail_cutoff).fillna(False).astype(float)

    co_crash = ret.lt(0.0).fillna(False).astype(float).mul(market_tail, axis=0)
    recent_co_crash = co_crash.ewm(
        halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=5
    ).mean()

    tail_days = market_tail.rolling(126, min_periods=80).sum()
    tail_propensity = co_crash.rolling(126, min_periods=80).sum().div(
        tail_days.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0
    )

    clustered_regime = market_tail.rolling(10, min_periods=5).sum().ge(2.0)
    return (
        recent_co_crash.mul(tail_propensity)
        .where(clustered_regime, 0.0)
        .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        .fillna(0.0)
    )


@register_factor
class TailClusterRefinancingForcedDeleveraging(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "tail_cluster_refinancing_forced_deleveraging"
    name = "Tail-Cluster Refinancing Deleveraging"
    category = "carry"
    description = (
        "Financing fragility multiplied by causal recent and historical "
        "market-tail co-crash pressure, activated only after clustered "
        "aggregate left-tail days."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "cash", "totalDebt", "debtGrowth", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        cash = data["cash"].reindex_like(close)
        debt = data["totalDebt"].reindex_like(close)
        debt_growth = data["debtGrowth"].reindex_like(close)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)

        financing_share = debt.abs().div(
            debt.abs().add(cash.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        bounded_debt_growth = debt_growth.clip(lower=-2.0, upper=2.0)
        fragility = (
            rank(financing_share)
            + rank(bounded_debt_growth)
        ) / 2.0

        tail_pressure = _tail_cluster_pressure(close)
        raw_signal = fragility.mul(rank(tail_pressure))
        neutral_signal = indneutralize(raw_signal, industry)

        return rank(neutral_signal).reindex_like(close).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Tail-Cluster Refinancing Deleveraging
programs.trading_idea: The parent’s negative realized IC is consistent with collection and financing fragility being a source of forced deleveraging during realized aggregate tail states, rather than a compensated six-day risk premium. Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks arrive in clusters; after multiple market-tail days, firms that co-crash and have weak cash coverage or rising debt are likely subject to continuing margin, mandate, and refinancing-driven sales. This should persist because balance-sheet liquidity is quarterly and difficult to hedge at the single-name level, while institutional deleveraging and collateral reallocation occur over several daily bars. The hypothesis is falsified if the negative conditional spread is absent after market-tail clusters, or if it remains equally strong during non-tail market regimes.
programs.description: Scores firms by financing fragility times a causal estimate of recent and historical co-crash exposure to market left-tail events. The signal is active only after a clustered market-tail regime and predicts lower six-bar returns for high values.

programs.code:
"""Product-design irreversibility under nonlinear aggregate tail risk.

Mechanism: heavy-tailed consumption shocks are especially costly for firms whose
product demand is design-intensive and whose economic capital is hard to
redeploy.  Excess lower-tail co-crash probability identifies nonlinear bad-state
exposure rather than conventional beta; R&D intensity, margins, and low asset
turnover identify product-design irreversibility.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _excess_lower_tail_dependence(close: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal excess conditional co-crash probability over a trailing window.

    A market-tail day is defined using the trailing lower quintile of the
    equal-weighted market return.  For each name, the statistic is its
    conditional probability of falling below its own trailing lower quintile
    on those days, less its unconditional lower-tail frequency.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change()
    market = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)

    market_cutoff = market.rolling(window, min_periods=window).quantile(0.20)
    own_cutoff = ret.rolling(window, min_periods=window).quantile(0.20)

    market_tail = (market < market_cutoff).astype(float)
    own_tail = ret.lt(own_cutoff).astype(float).where(ret.notna())
    joint_tail = own_tail.mul(market_tail, axis=0)

    tail_days = market_tail.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    conditional_rate = joint_tail.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum().div(
        tail_days.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0
    )
    unconditional_rate = own_tail.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    return conditional_rate - unconditional_rate


@register_factor
class DesignIrreversibilityTailDependencePremium(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "design_irreversibility_tail_dependence_premium"
    name = "Design Irreversibility Tail Dependence"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral nonlinear market co-crash exposure concentrated in "
        "R&D-intensive, high-margin, low-turnover product-design businesses."
    )
    window_length = 126
    inputs = ["close", "rdToRevenue", "grossMargin", "assetTurnover", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)
        rd_intensity = data["rdToRevenue"].reindex_like(close)
        gross_margin = data["grossMargin"].reindex_like(close)
        asset_turnover = data["assetTurnover"].reindex_like(close)

        excess_tail = _excess_lower_tail_dependence(close, 63)

        # Design-intensive rents and low turnover proxy capital that cannot be
        # cheaply redeployed after a severe discretionary-demand contraction.
        design_irreversibility = (
            rank(rd_intensity.clip(lower=0.0))
            + rank(gross_margin)
            + rank(-asset_turnover)
        ) / 3.0

        vulnerability = rank(excess_tail) * design_irreversibility
        neutral = indneutralize(vulnerability, industry)
        return rank(neutral).reindex_like(close).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Heavy-tailed consumption-growth shocks should disproportionately damage firms whose product economics depend on discretionary, design-intensive demand and whose capital is difficult to redeploy. The child measures nonlinear lower-tail co-crash dependence with the market rather than ordinary downside beta, then concentrates that exposure in R&D-intensive, high-margin, low-turnover businesses that proxy for product-design irreversibility. This is falsifiable: high-score firms should underperform over the next six days primarily following aggregate lower-tail events, and the effect should be weak or absent among low-R&D, high-turnover firms. The edge can persist because rare-state demand elasticity and irrecoverable product-development costs are difficult to hedge precisely, while constrained investors reduce exposure only after tail dependence becomes salient.

It multiplies this nonlinear tail dependence by a cross-sectional product-design irreversibility proxy based on R&D intensity, gross margin, and low asset turnover, then industry-neutralizes the result.

programs.code:
"""Terminal execution reversal after liquidity replenishment.

Mechanism: repeated high-participation price pressure can be temporary dealer
inventory displacement rather than information.  If normalized intraday impact
falls while participation and directional coherence remain high, replenishing
liquidity is absorbing the schedule and its terminal inventory effect should
reverse over the following week.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _terminal_replenishment_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal proxy for temporary impact at the terminal execution phase.

    Price impact is measured per square-root relative participation.  Comparing
    the latest three bars with the preceding three bars makes declining impact
    an observable proxy for depth replenishment, without using future bars.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
    intraday_ret = safe_close.div(safe_open).sub(1.0)

    safe_volume = volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
    adv20 = safe_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    participation = safe_volume.div(adv20.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    participation = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)
    root_participation = np.sqrt(participation)

    signed_flow = np.sign(intraday_ret) * root_participation
    flow_sum = signed_flow.rolling(5, min_periods=4).sum()
    gross_flow = signed_flow.abs().rolling(5, min_periods=4).sum()
    directional_pressure = flow_sum.div(gross_flow.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    coherence = directional_pressure.abs().clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    impact = intraday_ret.abs().div(
        np.sqrt(participation.clip(lower=0.05))
    )
    recent_impact = impact.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    prior_impact = recent_impact.shift(3)
    impact_decay = prior_impact.sub(recent_impact).div(
        prior_impact.add(recent_impact).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    )
    impact_decay = impact_decay.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    recent_activity = participation.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    activity_gate = np.tanh(recent_activity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0))

    # Reverse only pressure that is both coherent and losing marginal impact.
    return -directional_pressure * coherence * impact_decay * activity_gate


@register_factor
class ReplenishedImpactTerminalInventoryReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "replenished_impact_terminal_inventory_reversal"
    name = "Replenished Impact Terminal Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Reverses coherent, high-participation intraday pressure only when "
        "its price impact per square-root relative volume is declining, a "
        "proxy for terminal execution and liquidity replenishment."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        signal = _terminal_replenishment_score(
            data["close"], data["open"], data["volume"]
        )
        return rank(signal).fillna(0.5).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Persistent same-signed, high-participation intraday pressure is not necessarily evidence of unfinished informed demand: when its normalized price impact declines while participation remains high, liquidity replenishment is increasingly absorbing the execution schedule and the remaining move is predominantly temporary dealer inventory displacement. The child therefore trades against the direction of coherent pressure only in this terminal, declining-impact state, rather than flipping the parent universally. This is falsifiable: the reversal should occur after sustained participation with falling return-per-participation, but should disappear or become continuation when impact efficiency remains elevated; the edge can persist because latent execution completion and dealer inventory are not directly observable from daily bars and are costly to arbitrage under uncertain remaining order flow.
programs.description: Computes coherent signed intraday pressure from relative volume participation, then identifies terminal execution states where the recent intraday price impact per square-root participation is below its preceding level. The factor is positive after exhausted sell pressure and negative after exhausted buy pressure.

programs.code:
"""Earnings turnover impedance: delayed price discovery after disagreement auctions.

Mechanism: a fresh earnings surprise with exceptional turnover but little immediate
price displacement indicates that informed demand is being temporarily matched by
opposing inventory rather than incorporated into the midpoint.  Once this inventory
is redistributed, the price should resolve in the direction of the reported surprise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _turnover_impedance_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally identify fresh report events with high turnover and muted impact."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    prior_volatility = ret.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
    standardized_move = ret.abs() / prior_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    standardized_move = standardized_move.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    volume_base = safe_volume.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=20).median()
    relative_turnover = safe_volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    relative_turnover = relative_turnover.clip(lower=0.0, upper=20.0)

    # High turnover with a small volatility-normalized displacement is a
    # disagreement/absorption state rather than simple news momentum.
    muted_displacement = 1.0 / (1.0 + standardized_move.pow(2))
    impedance = np.log1p(relative_turnover) * muted_displacement
    impedance = impedance.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    # EPS fields are point-in-time step functions.  A change marks newly public
    # report information; the prior estimate supplies a pre-event scale.
    surprise_changed = eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1)) & eps_surprise.notna()
    actual_changed = eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1)) & eps_actual.notna()
    fresh_report = (surprise_changed | actual_changed).astype(float)

    prior_estimate_scale = eps_estimate.shift(1).abs()
    trailing_estimate_scale = eps_estimate.abs().rolling(8, min_periods=2).median().shift(1)
    scale = prior_estimate_scale.where(prior_estimate_scale > 0.01, trailing_estimate_scale)
    scale = scale.clip(lower=0.01)
    signed_surprise = (eps_surprise / scale).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
    signed_surprise = signed_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

    score = signed_surprise * impedance * fresh_report
    return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class EarningsTurnoverImpedanceResolution(BaseFactor):
    """Delayed earnings-price discovery conditional on turnover impedance."""

    factor_id = "earnings_turnover_impedance_resolution"
    name = "Earnings Turnover-Impedance Resolution"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of fresh signed EPS surprises when abnormal turnover "
        "is not matched by a proportionate volatility-normalized price response."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsSurprise", "epsEstimate", "epsActual"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _turnover_impedance_score(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["epsSurprise"],
            data["epsEstimate"],
            data["epsActual"],
        )
        return rank(score).fillna(0.5).astype(float)
programs.name: Earnings Turnover-Impedance Resolution
programs.trading_idea: A fresh earnings surprise accompanied by unusually high turnover but an abnormally small same-day price displacement represents a disagreement auction: informed investors trade against liquidity suppliers and slower discretionary investors without immediately moving the daily midpoint. The direction of the reported surprise should subsequently dominate as the temporary opposing inventory is unwound and investors who require time to interpret the report update positions. This is falsified if high-impedance surprise events do not deliver stronger six-day returns in the direction of the surprise than equally sized surprise events with immediate price displacement; the edge can persist because this conditional state is infrequent and cannot be identified from the surprise or volume alone.
programs.description: Ranks fresh EPS-surprise events by signed surprise magnitude times a turnover-impedance measure. Impedance is high when volume is far above its trailing baseline while the contemporaneous return is small relative to trailing volatility.

programs.code:
"""Temporary recovery bounces during clustered institutional selling.

Mechanism: a high close after a downside range shock can be dealer-facilitated
liquidity provision rather than completed absorption.  If downside shocks have
already clustered and participation is unusually high, an unfinished execution
schedule is likely to continue exerting sell pressure over subsequent days.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_downside_arrival_intensity(event: pd.DataFrame, halflife: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed intensity of prior downside-shock arrivals.

    The final shift ensures the intensity used for today's event contains only
    earlier arrivals, distinguishing a repeated sell schedule from an isolated
    daily dislocation.
    """
    return event.ewm(
        halflife=halflife,
        adjust=False,
        min_periods=halflife,
    ).mean().shift(1)


@register_factor
class RecoveryBounceSellScheduleContinuation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "recovery_bounce_sell_schedule_continuation"
    name = "Recovery Bounce Sell-Schedule Continuation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks recovery-shaped downside shocks by prior clustered downside "
        "arrival intensity and abnormal volume participation; high values "
        "indicate an unfinished institutional sell schedule."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        low = data["low"]
        high = data["high"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside_range = (1.0 - low / previous_close).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        # The scale is known before the current bar, preventing a shock from
        # normalizing itself away during volatile sell-program episodes.
        downside_scale = downside_range.rolling(
            30,
            min_periods=15,
        ).std().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_downside = downside_range / downside_scale
        event = (standardized_downside - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

        prior_intensity = _prior_downside_arrival_intensity(event, 4).clip(
            lower=0.0,
            upper=8.0,
        )

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        recovery = (2.0 * close_location - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        volume_base = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean().shift(1)
        abnormal_participation = (
            volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        # A clustered history and abnormal current participation are required:
        # isolated wick recoveries are not interpreted as scheduled execution.
        raw_signal = event * recovery * prior_intensity * abnormal_participation
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Recovery Bounce Sell-Schedule Continuation
programs.trading_idea: A close near the daily high after a large downside excursion is not necessarily genuine absorption: when it occurs amid an already clustered sequence of downside shocks and unusually high participation, it can be a temporary dealer-facilitated bounce during an unfinished institutional sell program. Execution constraints, benchmarked liquidation schedules, and limited displayed depth prevent such flow from being immediately arbitraged away, so the residual selling pressure should depress returns over the next six sessions. This hypothesis is falsified if high-scoring recovery bounces in high-participation downside clusters subsequently outperform rather than underperform the cross-section.
programs.description: The signal identifies a fresh downside-range shock that closes strongly off its low, then amplifies it only when prior downside shocks have elevated a causally estimated exponential arrival intensity and volume is unusually high. Higher values indicate likely continuation of an unfinished sell schedule and are expected to precede lower returns.

programs.code:
"""Uniform sell participation backlog: regular sell execution predicts continuation.

Mechanism: institutional execution algorithms commonly divide a parent sell order
into similarly sized participation slices.  Persistent downside pressure with low
day-to-day variation is therefore a daily-bar proxy for an uncompleted sell
schedule, whereas an isolated shock has low temporal coherence.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sell_schedule_score(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal proxy for regular, volume-participating sell execution.

    The volume baseline excludes the current bar.  Directional coherence is the
    trailing first moment divided by the trailing root-second-moment, so it is
    high only when downside participation recurs with stable magnitude.
    """
    previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close / previous_close - 1.0
    downside = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.50)

    prior_volume = volume.rolling(40, min_periods=12).mean().shift(1)
    participation = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    participation = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)
    pressure = (downside * participation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    mean_pressure = pressure.rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean()
    rms_pressure = np.sqrt(pressure.pow(2).rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean())
    coherence = mean_pressure / rms_pressure.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    return (mean_pressure * coherence).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class UniformSellParticipationBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "uniform_sell_participation_backlog"
    name = "Uniform Sell Participation Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks sustained volume-normalized downside pressure, weighted by its "
        "trailing temporal coherence, as a proxy for unfinished scheduled selling."
    )
    window_length = 55
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        score = _sell_schedule_score(data["close"], data["volume"])
        return rank(score).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Uniform Sell Participation Backlog
programs.trading_idea: A scheduled institutional sell program produces repeated downside bars with unusually stable volume participation, unlike a one-off information shock or panic liquidation whose daily pressure is irregular. The signal identifies names with both high recent downside participation and high temporal coherence of that participation, indicating that an execution backlog is likely still active and should predict negative six-day returns. This is falsifiable: conditional on the same cumulative downside pressure, high-coherence names should underperform low-coherence names; the edge persists because daily bars do not reveal the parent order's remaining quantity or execution schedule, while trading against it entails inventory and timing risk.
programs.description: Computes volume-normalized downside pressure and ranks the product of its trailing mean and directional coherence. High values represent persistent, regularly sized sell participation rather than isolated downside shocks.

programs.code:
"""Compressed recovery resilience from latent execution demand.

Mechanism: a downside excursion that closes near the high on high participation is
more likely to be genuine absorption when its range-per-participation is unusually
small. Persistent but regular elevated participation after the event is consistent
with a continuing latent buy schedule, so these names should outperform over the
next week.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_zscore(x: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal z-score whose reference distribution ends at t-1."""
    mean = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).mean().shift(1)
    std = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window // 2).std().shift(1)
    return (x - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class CompressedRecoveryExecutionResilience(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "compressed_recovery_execution_resilience"
    name = "Compressed Recovery Execution Resilience"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Longs high-volume downside-recovery bars whose price impact is "
        "compressed and whose participation remains regularly elevated, "
        "indicating absorbed supply and latent execution demand."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside = (1.0 - low / previous_close).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        downside_shock = _prior_zscore(downside, 40).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        recovery = (2.0 * close_location - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        recovery_persistence = recovery.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()

        volume_base = volume.rolling(30, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
        participation = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)
        persistent_participation = participation.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()

        log_participation = np.log(participation.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        participation_dispersion = log_participation.rolling(5, min_periods=3).std()
        regular_schedule = (
            persistent_participation / (1.0 + participation_dispersion)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)

        normalized_range = ((high - low) / previous_close).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        impact_per_participation = normalized_range / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        compression = (-_prior_zscore(impact_per_participation, 40)).clip(
            lower=0.0,
            upper=6.0,
        )

        raw_signal = (
            downside_shock
            * recovery_persistence
            * compression
            * regular_schedule
        )
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Compressed Recovery Execution Resilience
programs.trading_idea: The parent’s positive realized IC suggests that high-volume downside wicks closing near the high more often represent successful absorption than unfinished sell programs. This child isolates that interpretation by requiring unusually low range-per-participation (liquidity replenishment) and persistent, regular elevated participation after the recovery, consistent with a latent buy program being executed against temporarily supplied liquidity. The hypothesis is falsified if these compressed, regular recovery events do not outperform otherwise similar high-volume recovery events over the next six days; the edge can persist because latent execution schedules and effective depth are not directly observable from daily bars, while arbitraging them requires absorbing inventory and impact risk.
programs.description: Ranks downside-recovery bars by the combination of abnormal downside excursion, high close location, unusually compressed price impact per unit participation, and persistent regular elevated volume. High values identify absorbed sell shocks with evidence of continuing latent demand.

programs.code:
"""Issuance-validated estimate revision drift.

Mechanism: revisions to expected earnings are more informative when corporate
financing actions agree with their implication.  Net repurchases make an
upward revision more credible because managers commit capital at the current
valuation; net issuance weakens it and makes bad revisions more consequential.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _revision_with_financing_confirmation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    net_stock_issuance: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cross-channel revision score.

    Estimate changes use only a positive trailing lag.  Financing intensity is
    based on point-in-time reported issuance and is converted to a daily
    cross-sectional credibility rank, avoiding assumptions about comparable
    EPS or share-count scales across firms.
    """
    safe_close = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf, 0.0], np.nan)
    estimate = eps_estimate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    revision_yield = (estimate - estimate.shift(21)) / safe_close
    revision_yield = revision_yield.clip(lower=-0.10, upper=0.10)

    cap = market_cap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf, 0.0], np.nan).abs()
    issuance_intensity = net_stock_issuance.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / cap
    issuance_intensity = issuance_intensity.clip(lower=-0.20, upper=0.20)

    revision_rank = rank(revision_yield) - 0.5
    repurchase_credibility = rank(-issuance_intensity)
    return revision_rank * repurchase_credibility


@register_factor
class IssuanceValidatedEstimateRevisionDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "issuance_validated_estimate_revision_drift"
    name = "Issuance-Validated Estimate Revision Drift"

    prediction_horizon = 6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

            data["close"],
            data["epsEstimate"],
